Gaps between the existing seams and a read-only provider

Feasibility first: KidLibrary already depends on CatalogKit (Packages/KidLibrary/Package.swift:12-14, 19), and LibrarySource is MusicKit-free while MusicKitLibrarySource is public under #if canImport(MusicKit). A provider taking any LibrarySource in its initializer keeps the "only CatalogKit imports MusicKit" rule intact and stays stub-testable. A read-only provider can declare capabilities = []: reads (favorites(), playlists(), indexed()) go through readableProviders regardless of capabilities, while writes are filtered by canFavorite / .createPlaylists / mayEdit (MergedLibrary.swift:86-88, 405, 420, 436, 491-498).

Six things the plan will hit:

  1. No date on LibraryItem. FavoriteRow.favoritedAt is a non-optional Date; LibraryItem has no libraryAddedDate and MusicKitLibrarySource.libraryItem(from:) (:585-605) doesn't read one. Populating it needs a CatalogKit change.
  2. LibraryImport loses the library-id ↔ catalog-id mapping and the input order. resolved: [CatalogItem] is built by iterating songsByISRC (a dictionary, :542), and duplicate ISRCs collapse (songsByISRC[isrc] = item, :520). PlaylistEntryRow.position is "the order is the content", so tracks(of:) + resolveToCatalog cannot reconstruct a playlist's order without a CatalogKit change (return the mapping, or carry the ISRC through).
  3. Playlist identity. MergedLibrary merges playlists by handle.local: UUID and looks them up by local (:111-119, :491-498). An Apple-read playlist only has appleLibraryID; without a stable local it looks like a brand-new playlist on every read.
  4. Adoption is not implemented. The spec's step 3 ("write a CloudKit record with origin: appleLibrary", the-kid-s-library.md:207-208) has no code: reviewed(), playlists() and mergedFavoriteRows() are all read-only unions. Where adoption lives is an open design decision, and LibraryProvider has no write-back hook for it beyond addFavorite(origin:).
  5. No offset / single page. LibrarySource takes limit only; every MusicLibraryRequest sets request.limit (:404, 410, 428, 442, 465). Deep libraries need a limit policy, not paging.
  6. Ancestry names. The ISRC match returns ancestor ids and album rating, no names (:616-640), while LibraryAncestry wants names. A provider returning ancestry: .none gets topped up by MergedLibrary.toppedUpAncestry (:715-748), but that calls provider.recordAncestry(_:), whose default is a no-op (LibraryProvider.swift:92) — so a read-only Apple provider re-pays that round trip on every read unless it names lineage itself.

One more operational note: reviewed() converts a provider throw into .failed(String) and shows it to the parent, so the provider should throw when hasCloudLibraryEnabled == false rather than return [] — CatalogSource.swift:102 says exactly that ("say so, don't show an empty list"). And Session builds MergedLibrary with [CloudKitLibraryProvider(...)] at three sites — Session.swift:585, :1023 (reviewLibrary(for:), the admin path), and :2623 — all three need the new provider or the admin read will report it as unconfigured. 11182136310288

/// Decides what one kid may see or play; every surface must ask this.
public struct PolicyEngine: Sendable {
    public let policy: Policy

    private let allowed: Set<CatalogID>
    private let denied: Set<CatalogID>

    public init(policy: Policy) {
        self.policy = policy

        var allowed: Set<CatalogID> = []
        var denied: Set<CatalogID> = []
        for entry in policy.entries {
            switch entry.kind {
            case .allow: allowed.insert(entry.id)
            case .deny: denied.insert(entry.id)
            }
        }
        self.allowed = allowed
        self.denied = denied
    }

    /// Judge one item. Synchronous, no I/O — the caller supplies ancestry.
    public func evaluate(_ item: Item) -> Verdict {
        // Deny wins in every mode; a deny on a container reaches everything inside.
        if let match = firstDenied(item) {
            return .blocked(.deniedByParent(match))
        }

        switch policy.mode {
        case .reportOnly:
            // Rule 2. No walls. Activity is still logged by the caller.
            return .allowed

        case .allowOnly:
            // Level 1: no rating check — a parent hand-pick means it either way.
            return isListedAllowed(item) ? .allowed : .blocked(.notOnAllowList)

        case .denyPlusAuto:
            // Level 2: item-level allow overrides rating; container-level allow does not.
            if allowed.contains(item.id) {
                return .allowed
            }
            return ratingVerdict(for: item)
        }
    }

            return item.id
        }
        return item.ancestors.first { denied.contains($0.id) }?.id

    ) -> AsyncThrowingStream<KindedResults, any Error> {
        AsyncThrowingStream { continuation in
            let task = Task {
                var latest = KindedResults(byKind: [:])

                // `byKind` non-empty is what "the kid settled on this term"
                // actually means, and it is the test both exits below apply. A
                // term replaced by more typing before any kind landed was never
                // a search from the kid's point of view and stays out of the
                // report, which is the trade this file always intended. A term
                // whose results reached the screen is a search they made,
                // whether or not the remaining kinds ever arrived.

                do {
                    for try await snapshot in catalog.searchIncrementally(
                        term: term, budgets: budgets
                    ) {
                        latest = snapshot
                        continuation.yield(snapshot)
                    }
                } catch {
                    // Cancellation is not a failure, it is a teardown, and it is
                    // the common case: artists land first and the screen shows
                    // results while songs are still paging, so anything that
                    // ends the search — tapping into a result, the field
                    // clearing, a parent opening the admin to go and read the
                    // report — arrives mid-flight. Logging only on a clean run
                    // meant those searches were never recorded at all, which is
                    // the one thing the report cannot afford to be missing.
                    if Task.isCancelled {
                        if !latest.byKind.isEmpty { logSearch(term: term, results: latest) }
                        continuation.finish()
                    } else {
                        continuation.finish(throwing: error)
                    }
                    return
                }

                // Cancellation can also end the inner stream without throwing.
                if !latest.byKind.isEmpty { logSearch(term: term, results: latest) }
                continuation.finish()
            }
            // A kid typing a second term over the first drops this stream, and
            // dropping it has to stop the requests behind it rather than leave
            // them running to fill a page nobody is waiting on any more.
            continuation.onTermination = { _ in task.cancel() }
        }
    }

    /// Writes the search and everything it filtered out.
    ///
    /// Blocked results are logged even though the kid never saw them. They are
    /// the most useful line in a parent's report: they are how a parent finds
    /// out what their kid is curious about.
    ///
    /// **Once per term the kid settled on** — not once per kind, which would
    /// make one thing a kid did read as three searches in the report.
    ///
    /// "Settled on" means results for it reached the screen, not that every kind
    /// finished. A kid who retypes fast enough that nothing landed leaves no
    /// record of the first term, which is the right trade: a half-typed term
    /// they replaced themselves is noise. But a term whose results they *saw* is
    /// a search they made, and it is recorded even though the stream was torn
    /// down before the slower kinds arrived — which is what happens every time
    /// someone taps into a result, or opens the admin to go and read the report.
    ///
    /// The cost, stated because it is real: a torn-down search logs the counts of
    /// the kinds that had landed, so `resultCount` and `blockedCount` understate
    /// a search nobody waited out. A row with slightly low counts is worth far
    /// more to a parent than no row at all.
    private func logSearch(term: String, results: KindedResults) {
        eventLog.log(
            SearchEvent(
                term: term,
                resultCount: results.items.count,
                blockedCount: results.blocked.count,
                gaveUpEarly: results.gaveUpEarly
            ),
            for: kid.id
        )

        for blocked in results.blocked {
            // Filtered out before the page was drawn: the kid never saw these
            // and did nothing. Most of the block table is this.
            log(
                blocked.item,
                blockedFor: BlockReason(blocked.reason),
                reach: .unseen,
                origin: .search(term: term)
            )
        }
    }

    // MARK: - Playing

    /// Refused at the moment of playback, carrying why.
    struct Refused: Error {
        let reason: BlockReason
    }

    private var playingOrigin: PlaybackOrigin?

    /// Guards against writing the same play twice.
    ///
    /// A play is flushed from several places now — the track ending, a skip,
    /// starting something else, the app going to the background — because the

    /// that could own the job alone.
    private var currentPlayLogged = true

    /// Plays one item, **asking the policy engine again first**.
    ///
    /// It asks again rather than trusting that the UI only offered allowed

    /// not a safety failure — and this is the check that makes that true.
    func play(_ item: CatalogItem, origin: PlaybackOrigin) async throws {
        let verdict = try await catalog.verdict(for: item)

        if case .blocked(let reason) = verdict {
            let blockReason = BlockReason(reason)
            // They pressed play. One of the few block rows that describes
            // something the child actually did.
            log(item, blockedFor: blockReason, reach: .reached, origin: origin)
            throw Refused(reason: blockReason)

        logCurrentPlay()

        // with the kid, and nothing about it should delay the sound.
        await noteVisit(item, manner: .played)
    }

    /// Records that the kid got to something, and takes the new shelf back.
    ///
    /// **Awaited, unlike ``EventLog``**, and the asymmetry is the point. A

    /// change when a kid presses play reads as the tap having done nothing. It
    /// is a local insert on a background actor, on a path that already awaits a
    /// network round trip for the verdict.
    ///
    /// The trail comes back *from the write*. A caller that wrote and then
    /// fetched would be racing its own write — which is exactly the bug the
    /// Recent shelf had: the home screen reloaded microseconds after the write
    /// was handed to a detached task, usually before the row committed.
    ///
    /// On failure the trail is left alone rather than guessed at. The next
    /// arrival converges; a shelf that disagrees with the store would not.
    func noteVisit(_ item: CatalogItem, manner: VisitManner) async {
        let kidID = kid.id
        let visit = VisitEvent(
            itemID: item.id,
            displayName: item.title,
            artworkURL: item.artworkURL,
            albumID: item.ancestors.first { $0.id.kind == .album }?.id,
            artistID: item.ancestors.first { $0.id.kind == .artist }?.id,
            rating: StoredRating(item.rating),
            manner: manner
        )

        guard let trail = try? await recents.record(visit, for: kidID) else { return }
        // A parent can switch kids while this is in flight, and one child's
        // shelf must not land on another's screen.
        guard kidID == kid.id else { return }
        recentTrail = trail
    }

    func resume() async throws {
        try await player.resume()
    }

    /// Fetches what the next track will need while this one is still playing.
    ///
    /// **Nothing here is a decision.** No verdict is asked and none is cached:
    /// this warms a catalog fetch, and ``play(_:origin:)`` still judges the item
    /// immediately before any sound comes out of it. That ordering is what keeps
    /// a parent's deny landing mid-song from being defeated by a song that had
    /// already been fetched.
    ///
    /// Nothing is logged either. A preload is the app getting ready, not the
    /// child reaching anything — a visit is recorded when a track starts, which
    /// is the moment they actually hear it.
    func preload(_ item: CatalogItem) async {
        await player.preload(item)
    }

// MARK: - Library seeding

/// Reads the library for seeding; everything is matched to the catalog first.
public struct MusicKitLibrarySource: LibrarySource {
    private let catalog: MusicKitCatalogSource
    private let artworkSize: Int

    public init(artworkSize: Int = 512) {
        self.catalog = MusicKitCatalogSource(artworkSize: artworkSize)
        self.artworkSize = artworkSize
    }

    public func libraryItems(kinds: Set<ItemKind>, limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryItem] {
        var items: [LibraryItem] = []

        if kinds.contains(.song) {
            var request = MusicLibraryRequest<Song>()
            request.limit = limit
            let response = try await catalog.mapErrors { try await request.response() }
            items += response.items.map(libraryItem(from:))
        }
        if kinds.contains(.album) {
            var request = MusicLibraryRequest<Album>()
            request.limit = limit
            let response = try await catalog.mapErrors { try await request.response() }
            items += response.items.map(libraryItem(from:))
        }
        return items
    }

    public func searchLibrary(
        term: String,
        kinds: Set<ItemKind>,
        limit: Int
    ) async throws -> [LibraryItem] {
        var types: [any MusicLibrarySearchable.Type] = []
        if kinds.contains(.song) { types.append(Song.self) }
        if kinds.contains(.album) { types.append(Album.self) }
        guard !types.isEmpty else { return [] }

        var request = MusicLibrarySearchRequest(term: term, types: types)
        request.limit = limit
        let response = try await catalog.mapErrors { try await request.response() }

        var items: [LibraryItem] = []
        items += response.songs.map(libraryItem(from:))
        items += response.albums.map(libraryItem(from:))
        return items
    }

    // MARK: - Playlists and artists
    // Unverified: MusicKit isn't enabled on this App ID, so nothing here has run.

    public func libraryPlaylists(limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryPlaylist] {
        var request = MusicLibraryRequest<Playlist>()
        request.limit = limit
        let response = try await catalog.mapErrors { try await request.response() }
        return response.items.map(libraryPlaylist(from:))
    }

    /// Refetched by id — `MusicItemCollection` can't cross; videos drop silently.
    public func tracks(of playlist: LibraryPlaylist) async throws -> [LibraryItem] {
        var request = MusicLibraryRequest<Playlist>()
        request.filter(matching: \.id, equalTo: MusicItemID(playlist.id))
        let response = try await catalog.mapErrors { try await request.response() }
        guard let found = response.items.first else { return [] }

        let detailed = try await catalog.mapErrors { try await found.with([.tracks]) }
        guard let tracks = detailed.tracks else { return [] }

        return tracks.compactMap { track in
            guard case .song(let song) = track else { return nil }
            return libraryItem(from: song)
        }
    }

    public func libraryArtists(limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryItem] {
        var request = MusicLibraryRequest<Artist>()
        request.limit = limit
        let response = try await catalog.mapErrors { try await request.response() }
        return response.items.map { artist in
            LibraryItem(
                id: artist.id.rawValue,
                kind: .artist,
                title: artist.name,
                artworkURL: artworkURL(artist.artwork)
            )
        }
    }

    /// Votes over songs to survive name-search over-matching; ties ask the parent.
    public func resolveArtist(_ artist: LibraryItem) async throws -> ArtistResolution {
        guard artist.kind == .artist else { return .notInAppleMusic }

        let songs = try await searchLibrary(
            term: artist.title,
            kinds: [.song],
            limit: ArtistVote.sample
        )
        guard !songs.isEmpty else { return .notInAppleMusic }

        let matched = try await resolveToCatalog(songs)
        guard !matched.resolved.isEmpty else { return .notInAppleMusic }

        guard let winner = ArtistVote.winner(among: matched.resolved) else { return .ambiguous }
        guard let item = try await catalog.item(for: winner) else { return .notInAppleMusic }
        return .resolved(item)
    }

    private func libraryPlaylist(from playlist: Playlist) -> LibraryPlaylist {
        LibraryPlaylist(
            id: playlist.id.rawValue,
            name: playlist.name,
            curatorName: playlist.curatorName,
            trackCount: playlist.tracks?.count,
            artworkURL: artworkURL(playlist.artwork),
            // No `kind` means self-made; every case names something Apple built.
            isPersonal: playlist.kind == nil
        )
    }

    /// Matches by ISRC/UPC, two batched requests regardless of selection size.
    public func resolveToCatalog(_ items: [LibraryItem]) async throws -> LibraryImport {
        var resolved: [CatalogItem] = []
        var discarded: [DiscardedItem] = []

        var songsByISRC: [String: LibraryItem] = [:]
        var albumsByUPC: [String: LibraryItem] = [:]

        for item in items {
            switch item.kind {
            case .song:
                if let isrc = item.isrc {
                    songsByISRC[isrc] = item
                } else {
                    discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .noIdentifier))
                }
            case .album:
                if let upc = item.upc {
                    albumsByUPC[upc] = item
                } else {
                    discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .noIdentifier))
                }
            case .artist, .playlist:
                discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .unsupportedKind))
            }
        }

        var matchedISRCs: Set<String> = []
        if !songsByISRC.isEmpty {
            let codes: [String?] = songsByISRC.keys.map { $0 }
            var request = MusicCatalogResourceRequest<Song>(matching: \.isrc, memberOf: codes)
            request.properties = [.albums, .artists]
            findEquivalentsIfAvailable(&request)
            let response = try await catalog.mapErrors { try await request.response() }
            for song in response.items {
                if let isrc = song.isrc { matchedISRCs.insert(isrc) }
                resolved.append(catalogItem(from: song))
            }
        }

        var matchedUPCs: Set<String> = []
        if !albumsByUPC.isEmpty {
            let codes: [String?] = albumsByUPC.keys.map { $0 }
            var request = MusicCatalogResourceRequest<Album>(matching: \.upc, memberOf: codes)
            request.properties = [.artists]
            findEquivalentsIfAvailable(&request)
            let response = try await catalog.mapErrors { try await request.response() }
            for album in response.items {
                if let upc = album.upc { matchedUPCs.insert(upc) }
                resolved.append(catalogItem(from: album))
            }
        }

        // No match despite a code: delisted, regional, bootleg — discarded, named.
        for (isrc, item) in songsByISRC where !matchedISRCs.contains(isrc) {
            discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .notInAppleMusic))
        }
        for (upc, item) in albumsByUPC where !matchedUPCs.contains(upc) {
            discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .notInAppleMusic))
        }

        return LibraryImport(resolved: resolved, discarded: discarded)
    }

    /// Matches equivalent releases on OS 26.4+; older systems match more strictly.
    private func findEquivalentsIfAvailable<T>(_ request: inout MusicCatalogResourceRequest<T>) {
        if #available(iOS 26.4, macOS 26.4, tvOS 26.4, watchOS 26.4, visionOS 26.4, *) {
            request.options = [.findEquivalents]
        }
    }

    // MARK: - Mapping

    private func artworkURL(_ artwork: Artwork?) -> URL? {
        artwork?.url(width: artworkSize, height: artworkSize)
    }

    private func libraryItem(from song: Song) -> LibraryItem {
        LibraryItem(
            id: song.id.rawValue,
            kind: .song,
            title: song.title,
            subtitle: song.artistName,
            artworkURL: artworkURL(song.artwork),
            isrc: song.isrc
        )
    }

    private func libraryItem(from album: Album) -> LibraryItem {
        LibraryItem(
            id: album.id.rawValue,
            kind: .album,
            title: album.title,
            subtitle: album.artistName,
            artworkURL: artworkURL(album.artwork),
            upc: album.upc
        )
    }

    private func rating(from musicKit: MusicKit.ContentRating?) -> SandboxContentRating? {
        switch musicKit {
        case .clean: .clean
        case .explicit: .explicit
        case .none: nil
        @unknown default: nil
        }
    }

    /// Ancestry arrives attached; the match request already asked for it.
    private func catalogItem(from song: Song) -> CatalogItem {
        var ancestors: [Ancestor] = []
        if let album = song.albums?.first {
            ancestors.append(
                Ancestor(
                    id: CatalogID(.album, album.id.rawValue),
                    rating: rating(from: album.contentRating)
                )
            )
        }
        if let artist = song.artists?.first {
            ancestors.append(Ancestor(id: CatalogID(.artist, artist.id.rawValue)))
        }
        return CatalogItem(
            id: CatalogID(.song, song.id.rawValue),
            title: song.title,
            subtitle: song.artistName,
            artworkURL: artworkURL(song.artwork),
            rating: rating(from: song.contentRating),
            ancestors: ancestors,
            duration: song.duration,
            trackNumber: song.trackNumber
        )
    }

    private func catalogItem(from album: Album) -> CatalogItem {
        var ancestors: [Ancestor] = []
        if let artist = album.artists?.first {
            ancestors.append(Ancestor(id: CatalogID(.artist, artist.id.rawValue)))
        }
        return CatalogItem(
            id: CatalogID(.album, album.id.rawValue),
            title: album.title,
            subtitle: album.artistName,
            artworkURL: artworkURL(album.artwork),
            rating: rating(from: album.contentRating),
            ancestors: ancestors,
            isSingle: album.isSingle,
            trackCount: album.trackCount
        )
    }
}

    // MARK: - Reading, for the browser

    /// The whole library, judged once; the browser's only request.
    public func contents() async -> LibraryContents {
        var latest = LibraryContents.empty
        for await snapshot in contentsIncrementally() { latest = snapshot }
        return latest
    }

    /// The same library, paged; a final snapshot tops up lineage once.
    public func contentsIncrementally() -> AsyncStream<LibraryContents> {
        AsyncStream { continuation in
            let task = Task { @MainActor in
                let stored = await mergedRows()
                let indexed = await indexedRows()
                guard !stored.isEmpty || !indexed.isEmpty else {
                    continuation.yield(.empty)
                    continuation.finish()
                    return
                }

                var stored_ancestry: [CatalogID: LibraryAncestry] = [:]
                for row in stored where !row.ancestry.isEmpty { stored_ancestry[row.id] = row.ancestry }

                var latest = LibraryResults.empty
                for await snapshot in judged(stored) {
                    latest = snapshot
                    continuation.yield(
                        assemble(judged: snapshot, indexed: indexed, ancestry: stored_ancestry)
                    )
                }

                // Once, at the end — per-page would repeat the artist's name.
                let ancestry = await toppedUpAncestry(for: stored, judged: latest)
                continuation.yield(assemble(judged: latest, indexed: indexed, ancestry: ancestry))
                continuation.finish()
            }
            continuation.onTermination = { _ in task.cancel() }
        }
    }

    /// The browser's value; runs per page, so it must stay free of I/O.
    private func assemble(
        judged: LibraryResults,
        indexed: [LibraryIndexRow],
        ancestry: [CatalogID: LibraryAncestry]
    ) -> LibraryContents {
        var songs: [LibrarySong] = []
        var favoritedAlbums: [CatalogItem] = []
        var favoritedArtists: [CatalogItem] = []
        var blocked = judged.blocked
        var seen: Set<CatalogID> = []
        for item in judged.items where seen.insert(item.id).inserted {
            switch item.id.kind {
            case .song: songs.append(LibrarySong(item: item, ancestry: ancestry[item.id] ?? .none))
            case .album: favoritedAlbums.append(item)
            case .artist: favoritedArtists.append(item)
            // Unreachable: a playlist is never favorited — dropped, not asserted.
            case .playlist: break
            }
        }

        // Index comes second so a hand-kept favorite wins the resolved rating.
        var indexedAlbums: [CatalogItem] = []
        for row in indexed where seen.insert(row.catalogID).inserted {
            switch engine.evaluate(row.policyItem) {
            case .allowed:
                switch row.catalogID.kind {
                case .song:
                    songs.append(
                        LibrarySong(item: row.item, ancestry: row.ancestry, isChosen: false)
                    )
                case .album: indexedAlbums.append(row.item)
                default: break
                }
            case .blocked(let reason):
                blocked.append(BlockedItem(item: row.item, reason: reason))
            }
        }

        return LibraryContents(
            songs: songs,
            artists: LibraryBrowse.merged(favoritedArtists, LibraryBrowse.artists(from: songs)),
            albums: LibraryBrowse.merged(
                favoritedAlbums,
                indexedAlbums,
                LibraryBrowse.albums(from: songs)
            ),
            // chosenAlbums: only what the kid pointed at directly.
            chosenAlbums: LibraryBrowse.merged(
                favoritedAlbums,
                LibraryBrowse.albums(from: songs.filter(\.isChosen))
            ),
            blocked: blocked,
            isResolved: judged.isResolved
        )
    }

    /// Everything the index holds; judged from rating and lineage at index time.
    private func indexedRows() async -> [LibraryIndexRow] {
        for provider in readableProviders {
            guard let rows = try? await provider.indexed(), !rows.isEmpty else { continue }
            return rows
        }
        return []
    }

    // MARK: - Naming lineage

    /// Names lineage once, at the keep; a failed lookup still lets it land.
    private func ancestry(for item: CatalogItem) async -> LibraryAncestry {
        let ids = item.ancestors.map(\.id).filter { $0.kind == .album || $0.kind == .artist }
        guard !ids.isEmpty else { return .none }
        return Self.ancestry(from: ids, naming: await named(ids))
    }

    /// Tops up missing lineage; an artist favorite must never look unfilled.
    private func toppedUpAncestry(
        for stored: [Stored],
        judged: LibraryResults
    ) async -> [CatalogID: LibraryAncestry] {
        var out: [CatalogID: LibraryAncestry] = [:]
        for row in stored where !row.ancestry.isEmpty { out[row.id] = row.ancestry }

        let resolved = Dictionary(judged.items.map { ($0.id, $0) }, uniquingKeysWith: { a, _ in a })
        var parents: [CatalogID: [CatalogID]] = [:]
        var wanted: Set<CatalogID> = []
        for row in stored where row.ancestry.isEmpty {
            guard let item = resolved[row.id] else { continue }
            let ids = item.ancestors.map(\.id).filter { $0.kind == .album || $0.kind == .artist }
            guard !ids.isEmpty else { continue }
            parents[row.id] = ids
            wanted.formUnion(ids)
        }
        guard !wanted.isEmpty else { return out }

        let names = await named(Array(wanted))
        var learned: [CatalogID: LibraryAncestry] = [:]
        for (id, ids) in parents {
            let built = Self.ancestry(from: ids, naming: names)
            guard !built.isEmpty else { continue }
            learned[id] = built
            out[id] = built
        }

        guard !learned.isEmpty else { return out }
        for provider in liveProviders {
            try? await provider.recordAncestry(learned)
        }
        return out
    }

    /// Resolves identifiers to items purely to read their titles.
    private func named(_ ids: [CatalogID]) async -> [CatalogID: CatalogItem] {
        guard !ids.isEmpty, let items = try? await catalog.items(for: ids) else { return [:] }
        return Dictionary(items.map { ($0.id, $0) }, uniquingKeysWith: { first, _ in first })
    }

    /// An identifier is recorded only with its name, or it's never topped up.
    private static func ancestry(
        from ids: [CatalogID],
        naming names: [CatalogID: CatalogItem]
    ) -> LibraryAncestry {
        var out = LibraryAncestry()
        for id in ids {
            guard let named = names[id] else { continue }
            switch id.kind {
            case .album where out.albumID == nil:
                out.albumID = id.rawValue
                out.albumName = named.title
            case .artist where out.artistID == nil:
                out.artistID = id.rawValue
                out.artistName = named.title
                out.artistArtworkURL = named.artworkURL
            default:
                break
            }
        }
        return out
    }

        // here it insets nothing inside the stack — see

        // and which the root and every pushed screen both call. Adding the
        // reservation here as well is the doubling to watch for, not the fix.
        .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) { bottomBars }

        // it — the one thing a modal cannot be is half open, and this one is
        // dragged. It covers the bar and the toolbar because it is applied out
        // here, to everything — and now the search bar too, which is the one

        // thing ``KidPlayerModel/play(_:from:origin:)`` exists to prevent.

    /// The shelves themselves, lifted out of ``home`` only so the
    /// `ScrollViewReader` around them has one thing to wrap.
    private var shelves: some View {
        ScrollView {
            // Nothing to look at — somewhere to scroll to. A zero-height anchor
            // rather than the stack's own id, because "the top of the shelves"
            // is a fixed point and the stack is a thing whose height changes
            // every time a shelf loads.
            //
            // **Outside the spaced stack, not the first thing in it.** A child
            // of a `VStack(spacing: 24)` is worth 24 points of gap even when it
            // is worth no height, so as the first row it pushed every shelf down
            // by a shelf-gap of nothing.
            VStack(spacing: 0) {
                Color.clear.frame(height: 0).id(Self.homeTop)

                content
            }
            // Barely anything at the top: the toolbar is already a band of empty
            // above this, and a second one under it is the whole complaint.
            .padding(.top, 4)
            .padding(.bottom)
        }
    }

    private var content: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 24) {
            if !recents.isEmpty {
                Section {
                    TileShelf(session: session, items: recents, origin: .home) { item in
                        Task { await playSong(item) }
                    }
                } header: {
                    ShelfHeader(title: "Recent", route: .history)
                }
            }

            // "Library" means the kid's own favorites. It used to
            // label the list a parent built, which was the app telling a
            // kid that someone else's choices were their own.
            if !libraryItems.isEmpty {
                Section {
                    TileShelf(session: session, items: libraryItems, origin: .home) { item in
                        Task { await playSong(item) }
                    }
                } header: {
                    ShelfHeader(title: "Library", route: .library)
                }
            }

            if !session.playlists.isEmpty {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
                    Text("Playlists").font(.title2.bold()).padding(.horizontal)
                    PlaylistShelf(playlists: session.playlists)
                }
            }

            // One shelf per grown-up, named. Within each: what they suggested,
            // then what they allowed and have not suggested — one heading over
            // both, because the kid's question is *what did they pick for me*
            // and two headings answering it differently is the app showing its
            // own bookkeeping. Split across adults because two parents curate
            // separately, and a merged shelf would credit all of it to whoever
            // the app named first. A shelf rather than the wrapping grid this
            // used to be: the allow list was bounded by what a parent would type
            // into a list editor, and suggestions are not.
            ForEach(grownUpShelves) { shelf in
                Section {
                    SuggestedShelf(
                        session: session,
                        tiles: shelf.tiles,
                        onPlay: { item in Task { await playSong(item, origin: .suggestion) } },
                        onDismiss: dismiss
                    )
                } header: {
                    ShelfHeader(title: shelf.title, route: .suggestions(shelf.id))
                }
            }
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
    }

    /// The top of the shelves, as something `scrollTo` can be handed.
    private static let homeTop = "home-top"

    private var isHomeEmpty: Bool {
        recents.isEmpty && libraryItems.isEmpty && grownUpShelves.isEmpty
            && session.playlists.isEmpty
    }

    // MARK: - Loading

    /// Re-resolves the Recent shelf and nothing else.
    ///
    /// Cheap where the whole reload is not: the kid just tapped one of these, so
    /// `CachingCatalogSource` usually has every item warm and this costs no
    /// request at all. Separated because it now runs on every arrival rather
    /// than on the handful of moments the full reload was written for.
    private func reloadRecents() {
        Task {
            guard let items = try? await session.homeItems() else { return }

    private func reloadLibraryShelf() {

            // over the network — and awaiting them in turn made the wait their
            // sum when it only ever needed to be their maximum. Nothing here
            // depends on anything else here.
            async let recentItems = session.homeItems()
            async let favorites = session.favoriteItems()
            async let grownUp = session.grownUpShelves()
            (recents, libraryItems, grownUpShelves) = try await (recentItems, favorites, grownUp)
        } catch {
            trouble = Session.kidMessage(for: error)
        }
    }

import AdminGate
import SwiftUI

/// The passcode gate. Every route into the admin comes through here.
///
/// Two paths, decided by whether a passcode exists yet: choose one on first
/// run, enter it every time after. There is deliberately **no third path** —
/// no reset, no recovery, no "forgot it?". A reset a kid could drive is not a
/// gate, and this is the whole mechanism standing between a child and their own
/// settings.
///
/// That makes losing the passcode a dead end, which is the honest argument for
/// biometrics later rather than a back door now.
struct AdminGateView: View {
    @Bindable var session: Session
    var onOpen: () -> Void

    @State private var entry = ""
    @State private var confirmation = ""
    @State private var message: String?
    @FocusState private var focused: Bool

    /// **Which of the four states this device is in**, rather than the boolean it
    /// used to ask. `!isPasscodeSet` conflated three of them — see
    /// ``AdminGate/PasscodeEpoch``: a device that has never had a code, a device
    /// whose code was rotated elsewhere, and a Keychain that simply would not read.
    /// Only the first may be offered a chance to choose one.
    private var challenge: PasscodeChallenge { session.passcodeChallenge }

    private var isFirstRun: Bool { challenge == .choose }

    var body: some View {
        Form {
            if challenge == .unavailable {
                unavailableSection
            } else {
                entrySection
            }

            if let message {
                Text(message).foregroundStyle(.red)
            }

            if challenge != .unavailable {
                Button(isFirstRun ? "Set passcode" : "Unlock") { submit() }
                    .disabled(!canSubmit)
            }
        }
        .navigationTitle("Admin")
        .onAppear { focused = challenge != .unavailable }
    }

    /// **Offers nothing.** The Keychain could not be read, which says nothing about
    /// whether a passcode exists — and the one thing this screen must never do in
    /// that state is offer to replace it.
    private var unavailableSection: some View {
        Section {
            Label("Can't check the passcode", systemImage: "lock.trianglebadge.exclamationmark")
        } footer: {
            Text(
                "This device can't read its own keychain right now, so it can't tell whether a passcode is set. Locking the device and unlocking it again usually fixes it. Nothing has been changed."
            )
        }
    }

    private var entrySection: some View {
        Section {
            SecureField("Passcode", text: $entry)
                .focused($focused)
                .textContentType(.password)
                #if os(iOS)
                    .keyboardType(.numberPad)
                #endif

            if isFirstRun {
                SecureField("Confirm", text: $confirmation)
                    .textContentType(.password)
                    #if os(iOS)
                        .keyboardType(.numberPad)
                    #endif

        // admin, a playlist deleted, a favorite removed from the library

        .onChange(of: session.kid.id) { _, _ in

            // idle timeout the only thing between them and the allow list.

            // app switcher, a system alert, Notification Centre pulled halfway

            // takes both: writing the play event early costs nothing if they
            // come straight back.
            if phase == .background {
                session.closeAdmin()

public protocol CatalogAccess: Sendable {
    /// Prompt for access to Apple Music. Safe to call when already granted.
    func requestAuthorization() async -> AuthorizationStatus

    var authorizationStatus: AuthorizationStatus { get }

    /// Ask before promising anything, not at play time.
    func subscriptionState() async throws -> SubscriptionState

    /// Tracks a plan lapsing mid-session, a real case this needs to catch.
    var subscriptionUpdates: AsyncStream<SubscriptionState> { get }
}

public enum AuthorizationStatus: String, Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable {
    case notDetermined
    case denied
    case restricted
    case authorized
}

public struct SubscriptionState: Sendable, Hashable {
    /// The account can play catalog content.
    public let canPlayCatalogContent: Bool

    /// Offer a subscription — only behind a parental gate, never the kid's side.
    public let canBecomeSubscriber: Bool

    /// False means library reads return nothing; say so, don't show an empty list.
    public let hasCloudLibraryEnabled: Bool

    public init(
        canPlayCatalogContent: Bool,
        canBecomeSubscriber: Bool,
        hasCloudLibraryEnabled: Bool
    ) {
        self.canPlayCatalogContent = canPlayCatalogContent
        self.canBecomeSubscriber = canBecomeSubscriber
        self.hasCloudLibraryEnabled = hasCloudLibraryEnabled
    }
}

import Foundation

/// Short-lived seeding value; no library identifier is ever persisted or shown.
public struct LibraryItem: Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable {
    /// The library identifier. Meaningful only for the length of this flow.
    public let id: String

    public let kind: ItemKind
    public let title: String
    public let subtitle: String?
    public let artworkURL: URL?

    /// ISRC — the handle a library song is matched to the catalog by.
    public let isrc: String?

    /// Product code, on albums. The album equivalent of `isrc`.
    public let upc: String?

    public init(
        id: String,
        kind: ItemKind,
        title: String,
        subtitle: String? = nil,
        artworkURL: URL? = nil,
        isrc: String? = nil,
        upc: String? = nil
    ) {
        self.id = id
        self.kind = kind
        self.title = title
        self.subtitle = subtitle
        self.artworkURL = artworkURL
        self.isrc = isrc
        self.upc = upc
    }
}

---- LibraryImport

/// Why a library item could not be put on a list.
public enum DiscardReason: String, Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable {
    /// No code to match on — a ripped CD, upload, or dragged-in file.
    case noIdentifier

    /// Had a code but no match — regional gap, delisted, or bootleg.
    case notInAppleMusic

    /// Artists/playlists carry no code; a parent reaches one via a song or album.
    case unsupportedKind
}

/// Shown, not silently dropped — a parent expects to see what didn't seed and why.
public struct DiscardedItem: Sendable, Hashable {
    public let item: LibraryItem
    public let reason: DiscardReason

    public init(item: LibraryItem, reason: DiscardReason) {
        self.item = item
        self.reason = reason
    }
}

/// The outcome of matching a batch of library items against the catalog.
public struct LibraryImport: Sendable, Hashable {
    /// Catalog items, ready to go on an allow or deny list.
    public let resolved: [CatalogItem]

    /// What could not be matched.
    public let discarded: [DiscardedItem]

    public init(resolved: [CatalogItem], discarded: [DiscardedItem]) {
        self.resolved = resolved
        self.discarded = discarded
    }

    public static let empty = LibraryImport(resolved: [], discarded: [])
}

# Reading the Apple Music library, and grown-up mode

## Context

The kid's library has a provider seam (`LibraryProvider`) with one implementation, `CloudKitLibraryProvider`. The `.appleMusic` provider ID, the `origin: .appleLibrary` row origin, the two-provider merge, the shared-device gate and the admin's per-provider health readout all exist and are tested against a stub. The Apple Music provider itself does not exist, so nothing in the account's real library ever reaches a shelf.

This stage adds **reading** from the Apple Music library. No writes to Apple Music, and no adoption of Apple rows into our store. Two device cases, decided by the maintainer:

| Device | `DeviceLibraryState.isSharedDevice` | Kid mode reads | Grown-up mode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dedicated kid device (library is the kid's own) | `false` | CloudKit + Apple Music (merged) | Not offered |
| Shared device, or hand-me-down on a parent's account | `true` | CloudKit only (unchanged) | Offered behind the passcode: Apple Music library only, walls down, nothing logged |

Decisions already made (do not reopen):
- Grown-up mode reads the **Apple Music library only**. The kid's CloudKit favorites and playlists stay out of the adult's view.
- Grown-up mode has **no policy walls** and **writes nothing** to any kid's event log, Recent shelf or report. Same rule as the admin's preview methods.
- Grown-up mode is offered wherever `isSharedDevice` is true, hand-me-downs included.
- **No adoption.** Apple rows are read live on each pass and never stored. The shelf empties if the library becomes unreadable; the admin's health line says why.

## Design

### A. CatalogKit: the only MusicKit touch

Files: `Packages/CatalogKit/Sources/CatalogKit/LibrarySource.swift`, `Packages/CatalogKit/Sources/CatalogKit/MusicKitCatalogSource.swift` (the `MusicKitLibrarySource` at the bottom, inside `#if canImport(MusicKit)`).

- `LibraryItem` gains `addedAt: Date?`, populated from `libraryAddedDate` on `Song`/`Album`. Verify the property and its availability by compiling against the SDK; the floor is iOS 17 so iOS 16 APIs are fine.
- `LibraryImport` gains `matches: [String: CatalogItem]` keyed by library item id, so a caller keeps input order and per-item dates. `resolveToCatalog` keeps `[code: [LibraryItem]]` so two library items sharing an ISRC both map. `resolved` and `discarded` stay as they are (the suggestion editor uses them).
- `LibrarySource.libraryItems(kinds:limit:)` gains an `offset:` (defaulted, so existing conformers and stubs compile) using `MusicLibraryRequest.offset`, sorted newest-first via `sort(by: \.libraryAddedDate, ascending: false)`. Verify both compile. Newest first means a cap keeps the newest.

Nothing above changes the seeding flow's behaviour.

### B. KidLibrary: `AppleMusicLibraryProvider`

New file `Packages/KidLibrary/Sources/KidLibrary/AppleMusicLibraryProvider.swift`. `@MainActor final class`, `nonisolated let id = .appleMusic`, `nonisolated let capabilities: LibraryCapabilities = []` (read-only, so every write path in `MergedLibrary` skips it by the existing capability checks). Takes `source: any LibrarySource` and `access: any CatalogAccess` so it imports no MusicKit and is tested against stubs.

- **Snapshot, not a live query per call.** `Session.refreshLibrary()` runs on every heart tap and is documented as cheap. The provider holds an in-memory snapshot (`favorites`, `playlists`, learned `ancestry`, `readAt`) with a TTL of about ten minutes. The first `favorites()` awaits a full read; later calls return the snapshot and start one background refresh when stale. A `refresh()` is public for the app to call on foreground.
- **Read path.** `access.subscriptionState().hasCloudLibraryEnabled == false` throws `AppleLibraryUnavailable.cloudLibraryOff`, so `reviewed()` reports `.failed` with a real reason rather than an empty shelf. Otherwise page `libraryItems(kinds: [.song, .album], limit: 300, offset:)` up to a cap (songs and albums separately), `resolveToCatalog` each page, and map each library item through `matches` to a `FavoriteRow(id: UUID derived from the library id, catalogID: match.id, displayName: match.title, artworkURL, favoritedAt: addedAt ?? .distantPast, origin: .appleLibrary, ancestry: .none)`. Unresolved items are dropped, counted for the admin.
- **Artists are not read.** `LibraryBrowse.artists(from:)` derives artists from song ancestry, which is what the browser already does for CloudKit songs. Resolving library artists costs two requests each and is not worth it here.
- **Ancestry names** arrive through the existing `MergedLibrary.toppedUpAncestry`, which names lineage for rows whose ancestry is empty and calls `provider.recordAncestry`. The provider stores what it learns in the snapshot so the top-up is paid once per process.
- **Playlists** (a separate step, cuttable): `libraryPlaylists(limit: 25)`, personal ones only (`isPersonal`), `tracks(of:)` + `resolveToCatalog` per playlist, `PlaylistHandle(local: UUID derived deterministically from the Apple id, appleLibraryID:)`, `appleIsOurs: false`, `origin: .appleLibrary`, entries in track order. A deterministic `local` is what keeps the merge from seeing a new playlist on every read.

### C. Audience gating in `MergedLibrary`

File: `Packages/KidLibrary/Sources/KidLibrary/MergedLibrary.swift` (lines 71-88 today), plus a new `LibraryAudience.swift`.

- `public enum LibraryAudience { kid, grownUp }`. `MergedLibrary.init(..., audience: LibraryAudience = .kid)`.
- A pure `LibraryLiveness.status(of id:, device:, audience:) -> .live | .notReadable | .notLive` that both `liveProviders`/`readableProviders` and `reviewed()` use, so the admin's health line and the gate cannot disagree.
- Rules. Kid: CloudKit always live; Apple live iff `!isSharedDevice`, readable iff also `hasBeenAsked` (unchanged). Grown-up: Apple live and readable regardless of the device answers; CloudKit not live.
- In grown-up mode every write finds no writer and is a no-op; the UI hides the controls (see E).

### D. Session: grown-up mode

File: `Apps/AuralSandbox/AuralSandbox/Session.swift`.

- One `appleLibrary: AppleMusicLibraryProvider` held on the session (built from `MusicKitLibrarySource()` and `musicAccess`), so the snapshot survives mode switches and kid switches. It joins the provider list at all three `MergedLibrary` build sites (init, `reviewLibrary(for:)`, `rebuildEngines()`): `[CloudKitLibraryProvider(kid:context:), appleLibrary]`. On a dedicated kid device the existing gate now lets it through; on a shared device the gate keeps it out of the kid's reads exactly as the stub tests already assert.
- `private(set) var audience: LibraryAudience = .kid`, `var canListenAsGrownUp: Bool { deviceLibrary.isSharedDevice }`, and `var effectiveMode: SandboxMode` that returns `.reportOnly` in grown-up mode. The four `kid.effectiveMode` reads that gate search (`KidHomeView.swift:92`, `:548`, `Session.swift:1628`, `:1909`) move to it.
- `enterGrownUpMode()`: requires `isAdminOpen && canListenAsGrownUp`. Order matters, as in `switchTo(_:)`: `flushCurrentPlay()` first (the kid's play is theirs and is written), stop the player, then `audience = .grownUp`, a permissive `engine = PolicyEngine(policy: Policy(mode: .reportOnly, unratedBehavior: <allow>))`, `catalog = FilteredCatalog(source:engine:)`, `library = MergedLibrary(providers: [appleLibrary], ..., audience: .grownUp)`, `recentTrail = []`, `refreshLibrary()`.
- `leaveGrownUpMode()`: `discardCurrentPlay()` (the adult's play is never written), stop the player, `audience = .kid`, `rebuildCatalog()`, `loadRecentTrail()`.
- **Nothing logged.** `guard audience == .kid` at every write: `logSearch`, `logCurrentPlay`, `logBlocked`, `log(_:blockedFor:reach:origin:)`, `noteVisit`. `refreshSuggestions()`, `grownUpShelves()` and `homeItems()` return empty in grown-up mode.
- **Ends on background** (`scenePhase == .background`, beside the admin close in `KidHomeView`) and via the explicit control. Conservative on purpose: a device left on a table must come back in kid mode. The cost is that the adult's playback stops with the screen; flagged below.

### E. UI

- `AdminView.deviceSection`: a "Listen as a grown-up" button shown when `session.canListenAsGrownUp`. It calls `enterGrownUpMode()`, `closeAdmin()`, and dismisses the sheet.
- `KidHomeView`: when `session.audience == .grownUp`, a persistent band tinted `adminAccent` reading "Grown-up mode" with a "Back to kid mode" button (no passcode to leave). Recent, Playlists and the per-grown-up suggestion shelves are hidden; the Library shelf and search stay. Hearts and playlist-add controls hide behind a `session.canEditLibrary` flag (`audience == .kid`).
- `SharedDeviceOnboardingView` and the admin footer: the "kid's own" copy currently promises that favorites will be written to the child's Apple Music library. Reword to reading only ("whatever is already in your child's Apple Music library shows up here"). The "shared" copy gains one sentence: a grown-up can listen to their own library from the admin.
- `ReviewDetailViews` health strings: add the `cloudLibraryOff` failure wording.

### F. Docs (wiki, not READMEs)

- Wiki page *The Kid's Library* (`spec-restatement:ms4lu92o-01op-x3xmw`): record that the reading stage ships before the writing stage, without adoption, and add a grown-up mode section with the three decisions above. Update the "Staged plan".
- `CLAUDE.md`: the paragraph "The user's own library is not a browsing source unless the library is the kid's own" gains the second exception: a grown-up browsing their own library behind the passcode, with no kid policy and no logging.
- Verified MusicKit facts (`libraryAddedDate`, `MusicLibraryRequest.offset`, sort) go to *What We Know About MusicKit*.

## Steps

Each step builds, tests and commits on its own.

1. **CatalogKit contract.** `LibraryItem.addedAt`, `LibraryImport.matches`, `libraryItems(kinds:limit:offset:)` with a default; `MusicKitLibrarySource` populates all three. Contract test in `CatalogKitTests` via `StubLibrarySource`. Build `iphonesimulator` to catch availability.
2. **Audience gating.** `LibraryAudience`, `LibraryLiveness`, `MergedLibrary(audience:)`, `reviewed()` through the same table. Table-driven test in `MergedLibraryTests` (audience × device answers → which provider IDs are readable) and a grown-up case in `ReviewedLibraryTests`.
3. **The provider, favorites only.** `AppleMusicLibraryProvider` + a `StubLibrarySource` and `StubAccess` in `KidLibraryTests/Stubs.swift`. Tests: resolves songs and albums to catalog IDs; drops unresolved; `favoritedAt` from `addedAt`; cloud library off throws; second read reuses the snapshot; `recordAncestry` sticks.
4. **Wire it into Session** at the three build sites; the dedicated-kid device now merges. Onboarding and admin copy. `iphonesimulator` build.
5. **Grown-up mode in Session**: `audience`, `effectiveMode`, enter/leave, logging guards, background exit.
6. **Grown-up mode UI**: admin button, home band, hidden shelves and controls.
7. **Playlists** in the provider (cuttable): deterministic handles, ordered entries, tests.
8. **Docs**: wiki spec, CLAUDE.md paragraph, MusicKit facts.

## Verification

```sh
for p in Packages/*/; do swift test --package-path "$p"; done
cd Apps/AuralSandbox && xcodebuild build -scheme AuralSandbox -sdk iphonesimulator
```

On a device (the maintainer's, per CLAUDE.md), two checks that no test can make:
- Dedicated-kid answers: a song added in the Music app appears on the kid's Library shelf; an explicit one is absent from the shelf and shows in the admin review as a block.
- Shared-device answers: the kid's shelf is unchanged; unlock, "Listen as a grown-up", the Library shelf shows the adult's library and search has no walls; background the app and it returns in kid mode; the review for the kid shows no rows from the adult's session.

## Flagged for the maintainer

- **Background exit stops the adult's playback.** The alternative (stay in grown-up mode while audio plays) is one guard away, but leaves a walls-down player on a device a kid may pick up.
- **Deep libraries are capped**, newest first. The cap is a constant in the provider and the admin's health line should show the count read.
- **Unresolved items** (no ISRC/UPC or no catalog match) are dropped. The count is research question 2 measured continuously; it belongs on the admin's health line.

# Reading the Apple Music library, and grown-up mode

## Context

The kid's library has a provider seam (`LibraryProvider`) with one implementation, `CloudKitLibraryProvider`. The `.appleMusic` provider ID, the `origin: .appleLibrary` row origin, the two-provider merge, the shared-device gate and the admin's per-provider health readout all exist and are tested against a stub. The Apple Music provider itself does not exist, so nothing in the account's real library ever reaches a shelf.

This stage adds **reading** from the Apple Music library. No writes to Apple Music, and no adoption of Apple rows into our store. Two device cases:

| Device | `DeviceLibraryState.isSharedDevice` | Kid mode reads | Grown-up mode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dedicated kid device (library is the kid's own) | `false` | CloudKit + Apple Music (merged) | Not offered |
| Shared device, or hand-me-down on a parent's account | `true` | CloudKit only (unchanged) | Offered behind the passcode: Apple Music library only, walls down, nothing logged |

Decisions already made by the maintainer (do not reopen):
- Grown-up mode reads the **Apple Music library only**. The kid's CloudKit favorites and playlists stay out of the adult's view.
- Grown-up mode has **no policy walls** and **writes nothing** to any kid's event log, Recent shelf or report. Same rule as the admin's preview methods.
- Grown-up mode is offered wherever `isSharedDevice` is true, hand-me-downs included.
- **No adoption.** Apple rows are read live on each pass and never stored. The shelf empties if the library becomes unreadable; the admin's health line says why.
- **Grown-up mode ends only by the explicit "Back to kid mode" button.** Not on background, not on idle. A device left on the table stays walls-down until someone taps it; the band on screen is what says so.

## Design

### A. CatalogKit: the only MusicKit touch

Files: `Packages/CatalogKit/Sources/CatalogKit/LibrarySource.swift`, `Packages/CatalogKit/Sources/CatalogKit/MusicKitCatalogSource.swift` (`MusicKitLibrarySource`, inside `#if canImport(MusicKit)`), `Packages/CatalogKit/Tests/CatalogKitTests/StubCatalogSource.swift` (`StubLibrarySource`).

All additive, all defaulted, so the seeding flow and its stub keep compiling:
- `LibraryItem` gains `addedAt: Date?` (from `libraryAddedDate`) and `albumTitle: String?` (from `Song.albumTitle`). Both are iOS 16 / macOS 14 APIs, confirmed by the Plan agent against the SDK; the `iphonesimulator` build is the check.
- `LibraryImport` gains `matches: [String: CatalogItem]` keyed by library item id, so a caller keeps input order and per-item dates. `resolveToCatalog` keeps `[code: [LibraryItem]]` so two library items sharing an ISRC both map. The match runs from the response's `song.isrc` / `album.upc` back to the library items with that code, because `catalogItem(from:)` does not carry codes. `resolved` and `discarded` stay unchanged.
- `LibrarySource.libraryItems(kinds:limit:offset:)` with `offset = 0` defaulted, via `MusicLibraryRequest.offset`, sorted `sort(by: \.libraryAddedDate, ascending: false)`. Newest first means a cap keeps the newest.

Tests in `LibrarySeedingTests`: duplicate ISRCs both map, `matches` keyed by library id, input order recoverable.

### B. KidLibrary: audience gating in `MergedLibrary`

Files: `Packages/KidLibrary/Sources/KidLibrary/MergedLibrary.swift` (lines 71-88 today, and `reviewed()` at 295), new `LibraryAudience.swift`, `ReviewedLibrary.swift`.

- `public enum LibraryAudience { kid, grownUp }`. `MergedLibrary.init(..., audience: LibraryAudience = .kid)`.
- A pure `LibraryLiveness.status(of: LibraryProviderID, device: DeviceLibraryState, audience:) -> .live | .notReadable | .notLive(reason)` used by both the gate and `reviewed()`, so the admin's health line and the gate cannot disagree.
- Rules. Kid: CloudKit always live; Apple live iff `!isSharedDevice`, readable iff also `hasBeenAsked` (unchanged). Grown-up: Apple live and readable regardless of the device answers; CloudKit not live, reported as `ProviderHealth.notConfigured(.grownUpMode)` (new case; `ReviewDetailViews.describe` is an exhaustive switch and gains the wording).
- Walked with no CloudKit provider: reads all work; `addFavorite` finds no writer and succeeds silently (so hearts are hidden, see E); `createPlaylist` throws `LibraryUnavailable`; playlist edits no-op through `mayEdit`; `expand` no-ops.

Tests: audience × device table in `MergedLibraryTests` (`Harness(audience:)`), grown-up case in `ReviewedLibraryTests`.

### C. KidLibrary: `AppleMusicLibraryProvider`

New file `Packages/KidLibrary/Sources/KidLibrary/AppleMusicLibraryProvider.swift`. Same shape as `CloudKitLibraryProvider`: `@MainActor final class`, `nonisolated let id = .appleMusic`, `nonisolated let capabilities: LibraryCapabilities = []` (read-only; every write path in `MergedLibrary` already skips it on capability). `init(source: any LibrarySource, access: any CatalogAccess, cache: any ItemCache, limits:)` so it imports no MusicKit and is tested against stubs.

- **Snapshot, not a live query per call.** `Session.refreshLibrary()` runs on every heart tap and only asks for IDs and playlist rows, so a snapshot makes it cheap again. Holds `favorites`, `playlists`, `readAt`, `lastFailure`, and one `refresh: Task<Void, Never>?` so overlapping refreshes coalesce. First `favorites()` awaits a full read; later calls return the snapshot and start one background refresh when `readAt` is older than the TTL (ten minutes). `refresh()` is public for the app to call on foreground.
- **Read path.** `access.subscriptionState().hasCloudLibraryEnabled == false` throws `AppleLibraryUnavailable.cloudLibraryOff`, so `reviewed()` reports `.failed` with a real reason and the grown-up band can say so. Otherwise page `libraryItems(kinds:limit: 300, offset:)` for songs and albums separately up to a cap (500 songs, 200 albums until measured), `resolveToCatalog` each page, and build one `FavoriteRow` per library item through `matches`: `id` derived deterministically from the library id (SHA-256 of the id folded into a UUID), `catalogID: match.id`, `displayName: match.title`, `favoritedAt: addedAt ?? .distantPast`, `origin: .appleLibrary`. Unresolved items are dropped and counted on `lastRead` for the admin.
- **Ancestry filled at read time, not topped up.** `LibraryAncestry` built from `match.ancestors` ids, `artistName` from `LibraryItem.subtitle`, `albumName` from `LibraryItem.albumTitle`. `LibraryAncestry.isEmpty` is id-based, so `toppedUpAncestry` skips these rows and `LibraryBrowse.artists(from:)` derives the artist fold with no extra request. Artist artwork stays nil.
- **The cost is in `MergedLibrary.judge`, not the provider.** The favorites shelf and the library browser re-resolve every row through `catalog.items(for:)` at 30 per page. The provider already holds judgeable `CatalogItem`s from `resolveToCatalog` (rating and ancestor ids), so it `store`s each matched item into the shared `ItemCache` as pages land; `items(for:)` and `resolveAncestry` then hit cache. `Session` lifts its inline `InMemoryItemCache` (line 578) into a held property and passes it to both `CachingCatalogSource` and the provider.
- **Artists are not read from the library.** Resolving a library artist costs two requests each (the vote); the browser's artist fold covers it.
- **Playlists** (step 7, cuttable): `libraryPlaylists(limit: 25)`, personal only, `tracks(of:)` + `resolveToCatalog` per playlist, `PlaylistHandle(local: derived UUID from the Apple id, appleLibraryID:)`, `appleIsOurs: false`, `origin: .appleLibrary`, entries in track order. The deterministic `local` is what stops the merge from seeing a new playlist on every read.

Tests: new `KidLibraryTests/StubLibrarySource.swift` and a stub `CatalogAccess`; `AppleMusicLibraryProviderTests`: songs and albums resolve to catalog IDs; unresolved dropped and counted; `favoritedAt` from `addedAt`; ancestry names present without a top-up; cloud library off throws and sets `lastFailure`; second read reuses the snapshot (stub call count); stale snapshot refreshes once under concurrent reads; matched items land in the cache; playlist handles stable across reads.

### D. Session: one builder, and grown-up mode

File: `Apps/AuralSandbox/AuralSandbox/Session.swift`.

- One `appleLibrary: AppleMusicLibraryProvider` held on the session (from `MusicKitLibrarySource()`, `musicAccess`, the held cache), so the snapshot survives mode and kid switches. It joins the kid's provider list `[CloudKitLibraryProvider(kid:context:), appleLibrary]` in `rebuildEngines()` and in `reviewLibrary(for:)`. On a dedicated kid device the existing gate lets it through; on a shared device the gate keeps it out of the kid's reads, exactly as the stub tests already assert.
- **`rebuildEngines()` becomes audience-aware and the only builder.** It is called from `setMode`, `setUnratedBehavior`, `switchTo`, suggestion dismissal, list edits and sync-driven history clears; if it stayed kid-only, any of those firing during grown-up mode would silently put the adult back on the kid's engine under a band still saying grown-up. In `.grownUp` it builds `PolicyEngine(policy: Policy(mode: .reportOnly))` (allows everything; `unratedBehavior` is never consulted in that mode, say so in a comment), `FilteredCatalog` over it, and `MergedLibrary(providers: [appleLibrary], ..., audience: .grownUp)`. `reviewLibrary(for:)` stays kid-only.
- `private(set) var audience: LibraryAudience = .kid`; `var canListenAsGrownUp: Bool { deviceLibrary.isSharedDevice && hasCloudLibrary != false }` (tri-state: hidden only on a definite false, like the suggestion editor); `var canEditLibrary: Bool { audience == .kid }`; `var effectiveMode: SandboxMode` returning `.reportOnly` in grown-up mode. The four `kid.effectiveMode` search gates (`KidHomeView.swift:92`, `:548`, `Session.swift:1628`, `:1909`) move to it.
- `enterGrownUpMode()`: requires `isAdminOpen && canListenAsGrownUp`. Order, as in `switchTo(_:)`: `flushCurrentPlay()` (the kid's play is theirs and is written), then `audience = .grownUp`, `rebuildCatalog()`, `recentTrail = []`. The player reacts through `KidPlayerModel` (below).
- `leaveGrownUpMode()`: `discardCurrentPlay()` (the adult's play is never written), `audience = .kid`, `rebuildCatalog()`, `loadRecentTrail()`. The player must be stopped before `rebuildCatalog()` bumps `policyGeneration`, or `revalidatePlaying()` judges the adult's track on the kid engine and `refuseAdopted` logs a block under the kid. `Session` stops the player itself here rather than relying on the view.
- **Nothing logged.** `guard audience == .kid` on every path that writes under `kid.id`: `logSearch`, `logCurrentPlay` (covers `flushCurrentPlay`, `adoptNext`), `logBlocked`, `log(_:blockedFor:reach:origin:)`, `refuseAdopted`, `noteVisit`. `loadRecentTrail()` (also reached from `syncPass → absorbActivity`) does not repopulate `recentTrail` in grown-up mode. `homeItems()`, `grownUpShelves()` and `refreshSuggestions()` return empty in grown-up mode.
- **Entering the admin leaves grown-up mode.** The admin's kid switch, policy edits and review are about a kid; the lock button on the band calls `leaveGrownUpMode()` before opening the gate. Simplest rule and easy to state.
- **`KidPlayerModel` queue ownership.** `owner` is `session.kid.id` at `play` and in `switchedKid()`, and `save()` runs from the watchdog and `flush()`. Reusing `switchedKid()` for a mode change would restore the kid's queue onto the adult's bar on entry and write the adult's queue into the kid's slot on exit. So `owner` becomes `UUID?` (nil means never persist or restore) and a new `audienceChanged()` stops playback, clears the queue and sets `owner` to nil in grown-up mode or back to the kid on return. Driven by `.onChange(of: session.audience)` in `KidHomeView`, next to the existing `.onChange(of: session.kid.id)`.

### E. UI

- `AdminView.deviceSection`: a "Listen as a grown-up" button shown when `session.canListenAsGrownUp`. It calls `enterGrownUpMode()`, `closeAdmin()`, and dismisses the sheet.
- `KidHomeView`: when `session.audience == .grownUp`, a persistent band tinted `adminAccent` reading "Grown-up mode" with a "Back to kid mode" button (no passcode to leave). Recent, Playlists (until step 7) and the per-grown-up suggestion shelves are hidden; the Library shelf and search stay. When `appleLibrary.lastFailure` is set the band says why the shelf is empty (cloud library off, no network).
- Hearts and playlist controls hide behind `session.canEditLibrary`. Sites the Plan agent found: `AlbumView` 217, `ArtistView` 60, `KidHomeView` 1286, `NowPlayingView` 356 and 384, `NowPlayingBar` 119, `RecentRows` 33 and 101, `PlaylistView` 82.
- `SharedDeviceOnboardingView` (96-101) and the admin footer currently promise that favorites will be written to the child's Apple Music library. Reword to reading only ("whatever is already in your child's Apple Music library shows up here"). The "shared" copy gains one sentence: a grown-up can listen to their own library from the admin.

### F. Docs (wiki, not READMEs)

- Wiki *The Kid's Library* (`spec-restatement:ms4lu92o-01op-x3xmw`): the reading stage ships before the writing stage and without adoption; add a grown-up mode section with the decisions above; amend the invariants "isSharedDevice is the only input to which providers are live" (audience is now the second) and "it never appears on the kid's side" (the band is on the kid screen by design, in grown-up mode only). Note that "reporting runs in all three levels" does not extend to grown-up mode.
- `CLAUDE.md`: the paragraph "The user's own library is not a browsing source unless the library is the kid's own" gains the second exception: a grown-up browsing their own library behind the passcode, no kid policy, nothing logged.
- Verified MusicKit facts (`libraryAddedDate`, `Song.albumTitle`, `MusicLibraryRequest.offset`, the sort) go to *What We Know About MusicKit*.

## Steps

Each step builds, tests and commits on its own, per CLAUDE.md.

1. **CatalogKit contract** (A). `iphonesimulator` build for availability.
2. **Audience gating** (B).
3. **The provider, favorites only** (C, without playlists).
4. **Session wiring**: held cache and provider, audience-aware `rebuildEngines()`, the provider in the kid's list. The dedicated-kid device now merges. Onboarding and admin copy. `iphonesimulator` build.
5. **Grown-up mode in Session and the player**: `audience`, `effectiveMode`, `canEditLibrary`, enter/leave in the stated order, logging guards, `KidPlayerModel.owner: UUID?` and `audienceChanged()`.
6. **Grown-up mode UI**: admin button, home band with failure wording, hidden shelves and controls, lock button leaves the mode first.
7. **Playlists** in the provider (cuttable), plus the Playlists shelf in grown-up mode.
8. **Docs**: wiki spec, CLAUDE.md paragraph, MusicKit facts.

## Verification

```sh
for p in Packages/*/; do swift test --package-path "$p"; done
cd Apps/AuralSandbox && xcodebuild build -scheme AuralSandbox -sdk iphonesimulator
```

On a device (the maintainer's, per CLAUDE.md), the checks no test can make:
- Dedicated-kid answers: a song added in the Music app appears on the kid's Library shelf and in the browser under its artist; an explicit one is absent from the shelf and shows in the admin review as a block. Row counts and the unresolved count are what to report.
- Shared-device answers: the kid's shelf is unchanged. Unlock, "Listen as a grown-up": the Library shelf shows the adult's library, search has no walls, the heart is gone. Lock the phone mid-song: playback continues and the band is still there on return. Tap "Back to kid mode": playback stops, the kid's shelves return. The kid's review shows no rows from the adult's session.
- Turn iCloud Music Library off on the account: the band explains the empty shelf; the admin's health line says the same.

## Flagged for the maintainer

- **Grown-up mode has no timeout.** By decision. The band is the only signal, and a kid who picks up the phone sees a walls-down player until someone taps the button.
- **Deep libraries are capped**, newest first (500 songs, 200 albums as constants in the provider, to be raised once measured). The admin's health line should show what was read and what was dropped.
- **Unresolved items** (no ISRC/UPC, or no catalog match) are dropped. That count is research question 2 measured continuously, and it belongs on the health line.
- **Two wiki sentences become misnomers**: `LibraryOrigin.appleLibrary`'s doc says "adopted", and `ReviewedLibrary.adopted` is now "read from the Apple library this pass". Renaming is cosmetic and left out; the spec update says so.
