## Approved Plan:
# Reading the Apple Music library, and grown-up mode

## Context

The kid's library has a provider seam (`LibraryProvider`) with one implementation, `CloudKitLibraryProvider`. The `.appleMusic` provider ID, the `origin: .appleLibrary` row origin, the two-provider merge, the shared-device gate and the admin's per-provider health readout all exist and are tested against a stub. The Apple Music provider itself does not exist, so nothing in the account's real library ever reaches a shelf.

This stage adds **reading** from the Apple Music library. No writes to Apple Music, and no adoption of Apple rows into our store. Two device cases:

| Device | `DeviceLibraryState.isSharedDevice` | Kid mode reads | Grown-up mode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dedicated kid device (library is the kid's own) | `false` | CloudKit + Apple Music (merged) | Not offered |
| Shared device, or hand-me-down on a parent's account | `true` | CloudKit only (unchanged) | Offered behind the passcode: Apple Music library only, walls down, nothing logged |

Decisions already made by the maintainer (do not reopen):
- Grown-up mode reads the **Apple Music library only**. The kid's CloudKit favorites and playlists stay out of the adult's view.
- Grown-up mode has **no policy walls** and **writes nothing** to any kid's event log, Recent shelf or report. Same rule as the admin's preview methods.
- Grown-up mode is offered wherever `isSharedDevice` is true, hand-me-downs included.
- **No adoption.** Apple rows are read live on each pass and never stored. The shelf empties if the library becomes unreadable; the admin's health line says why.
- **Grown-up mode ends only by the explicit "Back to kid mode" button.** Not on background, not on idle. A device left on the table stays walls-down until someone taps it; the band on screen is what says so.

## Design

### A. CatalogKit: the only MusicKit touch

Files: `Packages/CatalogKit/Sources/CatalogKit/LibrarySource.swift`, `Packages/CatalogKit/Sources/CatalogKit/MusicKitCatalogSource.swift` (`MusicKitLibrarySource`, inside `#if canImport(MusicKit)`), `Packages/CatalogKit/Tests/CatalogKitTests/StubCatalogSource.swift` (`StubLibrarySource`).

All additive, all defaulted, so the seeding flow and its stub keep compiling:
- `LibraryItem` gains `addedAt: Date?` (from `libraryAddedDate`) and `albumTitle: String?` (from `Song.albumTitle`). Both are iOS 16 / macOS 14 APIs, confirmed by the Plan agent against the SDK; the `iphonesimulator` build is the check.
- `LibraryImport` gains `matches: [String: CatalogItem]` keyed by library item id, so a caller keeps input order and per-item dates. `resolveToCatalog` keeps `[code: [LibraryItem]]` so two library items sharing an ISRC both map. The match runs from the response's `song.isrc` / `album.upc` back to the library items with that code, because `catalogItem(from:)` does not carry codes. `resolved` and `discarded` stay unchanged.
- `LibrarySource.libraryItems(kinds:limit:offset:)` with `offset = 0` defaulted, via `MusicLibraryRequest.offset`, sorted `sort(by: \.libraryAddedDate, ascending: false)`. Newest first means a cap keeps the newest.

Tests in `LibrarySeedingTests`: duplicate ISRCs both map, `matches` keyed by library id, input order recoverable.

### B. KidLibrary: audience gating in `MergedLibrary`

Files: `Packages/KidLibrary/Sources/KidLibrary/MergedLibrary.swift` (lines 71-88 today, and `reviewed()` at 295), new `LibraryAudience.swift`, `ReviewedLibrary.swift`.

- `public enum LibraryAudience { kid, grownUp }`. `MergedLibrary.init(..., audience: LibraryAudience = .kid)`.
- A pure `LibraryLiveness.status(of: LibraryProviderID, device: DeviceLibraryState, audience:) -> .live | .notReadable | .notLive(reason)` used by both the gate and `reviewed()`, so the admin's health line and the gate cannot disagree.
- Rules. Kid: CloudKit always live; Apple live iff `!isSharedDevice`, readable iff also `hasBeenAsked` (unchanged). Grown-up: Apple live and readable regardless of the device answers; CloudKit not live, reported as `ProviderHealth.notConfigured(.grownUpMode)` (new case; `ReviewDetailViews.describe` is an exhaustive switch and gains the wording).
- **The heart draws only from rows the kid can act on.** `MergedLibrary.favoriteIDs()` unions every readable provider, so on a dedicated device it would include Apple rows; `toggleFavorite` on one would see a filled heart, call `removeFavorite`, reach only CloudKit, find no row, and leave the heart filled forever. So `favoriteIDs()` narrows to providers that can favorite that kind (the writers), while `favorites()` and the browser keep the union. An Apple-only song shows on the shelf with an empty heart; tapping it makes a CloudKit favorite, which is a true statement about what the kid did.
- Walked with no CloudKit provider: reads all work; `addFavorite` finds no writer and succeeds silently (so hearts are hidden, see E); `createPlaylist` throws `LibraryUnavailable`; playlist edits no-op through `mayEdit`; `expand` no-ops.

Tests: audience × device table in `MergedLibraryTests` (`Harness(audience:)`), grown-up case in `ReviewedLibraryTests`, and a two-provider test that an Apple-only row is on the shelf but not in `favoriteIDs()` until the kid hearts it.

### C. KidLibrary: `AppleMusicLibraryProvider`

New file `Packages/KidLibrary/Sources/KidLibrary/AppleMusicLibraryProvider.swift`. Same shape as `CloudKitLibraryProvider`: `@MainActor final class`, `nonisolated let id = .appleMusic`, `nonisolated let capabilities: LibraryCapabilities = []` (read-only; every write path in `MergedLibrary` already skips it on capability). `init(source: any LibrarySource, access: any CatalogAccess, cache: any ItemCache, limits:)` so it imports no MusicKit and is tested against stubs.

- **Snapshot, never a blocking read.** `Session.refreshLibrary()` runs on every heart tap, and `KidHomeView.loadShelves()` awaits it before the home screen draws, so `favorites()` and `playlists()` must never wait on the network. They return the current snapshot (empty before the first read completes) and start one background refresh when `readAt` is older than the TTL (ten minutes). The provider holds `favorites`, `playlists`, `readAt`, `lastFailure`, and one `refresh: Task<Void, Never>?` so overlapping refreshes coalesce. `refresh()` is public and awaitable; Session owns the completion: `Task { await appleLibrary.refresh(); await refreshLibrary() }` in `start()` and on foreground. `KidHomeView.onChange(of: session.favoriteIDs)` and `LibraryView.swift:67` already reload on that change, so the shelf fills in with no new plumbing. This keeps the spec's "CloudKit rows on the first frame, no loading state" true.
- **Read path.** `access.subscriptionState().hasCloudLibraryEnabled == false` throws `AppleLibraryUnavailable.cloudLibraryOff`, so `reviewed()` reports `.failed` with a real reason and the grown-up band can say so. Otherwise page `libraryItems(kinds:limit: 300, offset:)` for songs and albums separately up to a cap (500 songs, 200 albums until measured), `resolveToCatalog` each page, and build one `FavoriteRow` per library item through `matches`: `id` derived deterministically from the library id (SHA-256 of the id folded into a UUID), `catalogID: match.id`, `displayName: match.title`, `favoritedAt: addedAt ?? .distantPast`, `origin: .appleLibrary`. Unresolved items are dropped and counted on `lastRead` for the admin.
- **Ancestry filled at read time, not topped up.** `LibraryAncestry` built from `match.ancestors` ids, `artistName` from `LibraryItem.subtitle`, `albumName` from `LibraryItem.albumTitle`. `LibraryAncestry.isEmpty` is id-based, so `toppedUpAncestry` skips these rows and `LibraryBrowse.artists(from:)` derives the artist fold with no extra request. Artist artwork stays nil.
- **The cost is in `MergedLibrary.judge`, not the provider.** The favorites shelf and the library browser re-resolve every row through `catalog.items(for:)` at 30 per page. The provider already holds judgeable `CatalogItem`s from `resolveToCatalog` (rating and ancestor ids), so it `store`s each matched item into the shared `ItemCache` as pages land; `items(for:)` and `resolveAncestry` then hit cache. `Session` lifts its inline `InMemoryItemCache` (line 578) into a held property and passes it to both `CachingCatalogSource` and the provider.
- **Artists are not read from the library.** Resolving a library artist costs two requests each (the vote); the browser's artist fold covers it.
- **Playlists** (step 7, cuttable): `libraryPlaylists(limit: 25)`, personal only, `tracks(of:)` + `resolveToCatalog` per playlist, `PlaylistHandle(local: derived UUID from the Apple id, appleLibraryID:)`, `appleIsOurs: false`, `origin: .appleLibrary`, entries in track order. The deterministic `local` is what stops the merge from seeing a new playlist on every read.

Tests: new `KidLibraryTests/StubLibrarySource.swift` and a stub `CatalogAccess`; `AppleMusicLibraryProviderTests`: `favorites()` before any refresh returns empty without touching the source; after `refresh()` songs and albums resolve to catalog IDs; unresolved dropped and counted; `favoritedAt` from `addedAt`; ancestry names present without a top-up; cloud library off sets `lastFailure` and `refresh()` throws; a fresh snapshot is served without a source call; a stale one starts exactly one refresh under concurrent reads; matched items land in the cache; playlist handles stable across reads.

Each step builds, tests and commits on its own, per CLAUDE.md.

- **Grown-up mode has no timeout.** By decision. The band is the only signal, and a kid who picks up the phone sees a walls-down player until someone taps the button.
- **Deep libraries are capped**, newest first (500 songs, 200 albums as constants in the provider, to be raised once measured). The admin's health line should show what was read and what was dropped.
- **Unresolved items** (no ISRC/UPC, or no catalog match) are dropped. That count is research question 2 measured continuously, and it belongs on the health line.
- **The heart means "kept in this app."** An Apple-library song on a dedicated device shows with an empty heart until the kid taps it. The alternative, a filled heart that cannot be emptied, is a dead control.
- **A level 1 kid on a dedicated device blocks their whole Apple library.** Every row judges `.notOnAllowList`, so `ReviewedLibrary.blockedFavorites` can hold hundreds of rows. That is the policy working, and the review screen was not built expecting the volume.
- **Two wiki sentences become misnomers**: `LibraryOrigin.appleLibrary`'s doc says "adopted", and `ReviewedLibrary.adopted` is now "read from the Apple library this pass". Renaming is cosmetic and left out; the spec update says so.

public struct LibraryPlaylist: Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable {
    /// Library id, meaningful only for this flow — like ``LibraryItem/id``.
    public let id: String

    public let name: String
    public let curatorName: String?
    public let trackCount: Int?
    public let artworkURL: URL?

    /// Self-made vs. Apple-curated; shown to the parent, resolution is unaffected.
    public let isPersonal: Bool

    public init(
        id: String,
        name: String,
        curatorName: String? = nil,
        trackCount: Int? = nil,
        artworkURL: URL? = nil,
        isPersonal: Bool
    ) {
        self.id = id
        self.name = name
        self.curatorName = curatorName
        self.trackCount = trackCount
        self.artworkURL = artworkURL
        self.isPersonal = isPersonal
    }
}

/// What came of trying to name a library artist in the catalog.
public enum ArtistResolution: Sendable, Hashable {
    case resolved(CatalogItem)

    /// Songs disagreed on an artist — a refusal, since a wrong guess grants reach.
    case ambiguous

    /// Nothing of theirs could be matched at all.
    case notInAppleMusic
}

/// A vote, not `song.artists.first` — wrong for guest credits and Various Artists.
public enum ArtistVote: Sendable {
    /// How many of an artist's songs to resolve before deciding.
    public static let sample = 10

    /// The share of resolved songs that must agree. A strict majority.
    public static let threshold = 0.5

    /// Empty ids drop before counting, or artists collapse onto one bogus winner.
    public static func winner(among songs: [CatalogItem]) -> CatalogID? {
        var counts: [CatalogID: Int] = [:]
        var voters = 0
        for song in songs {
            guard
                let artist = song.ancestors.first(where: { $0.id.kind == .artist })?.id,
                !artist.rawValue.isEmpty
            else { continue }
            counts[artist, default: 0] += 1
            voters += 1
        }
        guard voters > 0, let best = counts.max(by: { $0.value < $1.value }) else { return nil }
        return Double(best.value) > Double(voters) * threshold ? best.key : nil
    }
}

/// Why a library item could not be put on a list.
public enum DiscardReason: String, Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable {
    /// No code to match on — a ripped CD, upload, or dragged-in file.
    case noIdentifier

    /// Had a code but no match — regional gap, delisted, or bootleg.
    case notInAppleMusic

    /// Artists/playlists carry no code; a parent reaches one via a song or album.
    case unsupportedKind
}

/// Shown, not silently dropped — a parent expects to see what didn't seed and why.
public struct DiscardedItem: Sendable, Hashable {
    public let item: LibraryItem
    public let reason: DiscardReason

    public init(item: LibraryItem, reason: DiscardReason) {
        self.item = item
        self.reason = reason
    }
}

/// The outcome of matching a batch of library items against the catalog.
public struct LibraryImport: Sendable, Hashable {
    /// Catalog items, ready to go on an allow or deny list.
    public let resolved: [CatalogItem]

    /// What could not be matched.
    public let discarded: [DiscardedItem]

    public init(resolved: [CatalogItem], discarded: [DiscardedItem]) {
        self.resolved = resolved
        self.discarded = discarded
    }

    public static let empty = LibraryImport(resolved: [], discarded: [])
}

/// Seeding shortcut, not a bound on allow; a pick becomes an item or is discarded.
public protocol LibrarySource: Sendable {
    /// Songs and albums only — the only kinds that can match the catalog.
    func libraryItems(kinds: Set<ItemKind>, limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryItem]

    /// Search within the library.
    func searchLibrary(term: String, kinds: Set<ItemKind>, limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryItem]

    /// Batched — the one place a parent hands us hundreds of items at once.
    func resolveToCatalog(_ items: [LibraryItem]) async throws -> LibraryImport

    /// The account's own playlists, Apple's and the account holder's alike.
    func libraryPlaylists(limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryPlaylist]

    /// Tracks, not the playlist — it has no code; resolve yields catalog songs.
    func tracks(of playlist: LibraryPlaylist) async throws -> [LibraryItem]

    /// The account's artists. Names only — an artist carries no code.
    func libraryArtists(limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryItem]

    /// Names an artist via their songs' ISRCs and ancestry — see ``ArtistVote``.
    func resolveArtist(_ artist: LibraryItem) async throws -> ArtistResolution
}

extension LibrarySource {
    /// Defaults, not requirements, added later — like `topSongs(of:)` elsewhere.
    public func libraryPlaylists(limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryPlaylist] { [] }

    public func tracks(of playlist: LibraryPlaylist) async throws -> [LibraryItem] { [] }

    public func libraryArtists(limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryItem] { [] }

    public func resolveArtist(_ artist: LibraryItem) async throws -> ArtistResolution {
        .notInAppleMusic
    }
}

/// Resolves what the test says; the one rule that matters: no match, discarded.
actor StubLibrarySource: LibrarySource {
    private var library: [LibraryItem]
    private var catalogMatches: [String: CatalogItem]
    private var playlists: [LibraryPlaylist]
    private var playlistTracks: [String: [LibraryItem]]

    private(set) var resolveCallCount = 0

    /// - Parameter catalogMatches: keyed by ISRC/UPC; absent means not on Apple.
    init(
        library: [LibraryItem] = [],
        catalogMatches: [String: CatalogItem] = [:],
        playlists: [LibraryPlaylist] = [],
        playlistTracks: [String: [LibraryItem]] = [:]
    ) {
        self.library = library
        self.catalogMatches = catalogMatches
        self.playlists = playlists
        self.playlistTracks = playlistTracks
    }

    func libraryPlaylists(limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryPlaylist] {
        Array(playlists.prefix(limit))
    }

    func tracks(of playlist: LibraryPlaylist) async throws -> [LibraryItem] {
        playlistTracks[playlist.id] ?? []
    }

    func libraryArtists(limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryItem] {
        Array(library.filter { $0.kind == .artist }.prefix(limit))
    }

    /// The real shape without MusicKit: sample songs, let ArtistVote decide.
    func resolveArtist(_ artist: LibraryItem) async throws -> ArtistResolution {
        guard artist.kind == .artist else { return .notInAppleMusic }
        let songs = try await searchLibrary(
            term: artist.title, kinds: [.song], limit: ArtistVote.sample
        )
        let matched = try await resolveToCatalog(songs)
        guard !matched.resolved.isEmpty else { return .notInAppleMusic }
        guard let winner = ArtistVote.winner(among: matched.resolved) else { return .ambiguous }
        return .resolved(CatalogItem(id: winner, title: artist.title))
    }

    func libraryItems(kinds: Set<ItemKind>, limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryItem] {
        Array(library.filter { kinds.contains($0.kind) }.prefix(limit))
    }

    func searchLibrary(term: String, kinds: Set<ItemKind>, limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryItem] {
        Array(
            library
                .filter { kinds.contains($0.kind) && $0.title.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains(term) }
                .prefix(limit)
        )
    }

    func resolveToCatalog(_ items: [LibraryItem]) async throws -> LibraryImport {
        resolveCallCount += 1

        var resolved: [CatalogItem] = []
        var discarded: [DiscardedItem] = []

        for item in items {
            switch item.kind {
            case .artist, .playlist:
                discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .unsupportedKind))
            case .song, .album:
                guard let code = item.isrc ?? item.upc else {
                    discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .noIdentifier))
                    continue
                }
                if let match = catalogMatches[code] {
                    resolved.append(match)
                } else {
                    discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .notInAppleMusic))
                }
            }
        }

        return LibraryImport(resolved: resolved, discarded: discarded)
    }
}

    /// Matches by ISRC/UPC, two batched requests regardless of selection size.
    public func resolveToCatalog(_ items: [LibraryItem]) async throws -> LibraryImport {
        var resolved: [CatalogItem] = []
        var discarded: [DiscardedItem] = []
        var matches: [String: CatalogItem] = [:]

        // Arrays, not one item per code: a library holds the same recording
        // twice more often than you'd think, and both rows want their match.
        var songsByISRC: [String: [LibraryItem]] = [:]
        var albumsByUPC: [String: [LibraryItem]] = [:]

        for item in items {
            switch item.kind {
            case .song:
                if let isrc = item.isrc {
                    songsByISRC[isrc, default: []].append(item)
                } else {
                    discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .noIdentifier))
                }
            case .album:
                if let upc = item.upc {
                    albumsByUPC[upc, default: []].append(item)
                } else {
                    discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .noIdentifier))
                }
            case .artist, .playlist:
                discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .unsupportedKind))
            }
        }

        var matchedISRCs: Set<String> = []
        if !songsByISRC.isEmpty {
            let codes: [String?] = songsByISRC.keys.map { $0 }
            var request = MusicCatalogResourceRequest<Song>(matching: \.isrc, memberOf: codes)
            request.properties = [.albums, .artists]
            findEquivalentsIfAvailable(&request)
            let response = try await catalog.mapErrors { try await request.response() }
            for song in response.items {
                let item = catalogItem(from: song)
                resolved.append(item)
                // The match runs back from the response's code: the catalog
                // item carries none, and the library id is the caller's handle.
                guard let isrc = song.isrc else { continue }
                matchedISRCs.insert(isrc)
                for library in songsByISRC[isrc] ?? [] { matches[library.id] = item }
            }
        }

        var matchedUPCs: Set<String> = []
        if !albumsByUPC.isEmpty {
            let codes: [String?] = albumsByUPC.keys.map { $0 }
            var request = MusicCatalogResourceRequest<Album>(matching: \.upc, memberOf: codes)
            request.properties = [.artists]
            findEquivalentsIfAvailable(&request)
            let response = try await catalog.mapErrors { try await request.response() }
            for album in response.items {
                let item = catalogItem(from: album)
                resolved.append(item)
                guard let upc = album.upc else { continue }
                matchedUPCs.insert(upc)
                for library in albumsByUPC[upc] ?? [] { matches[library.id] = item }
            }
        }

        // No match despite a code: delisted, regional, bootleg — discarded, named.
        for (isrc, items) in songsByISRC where !matchedISRCs.contains(isrc) {
            for item in items { discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .notInAppleMusic)) }
        }
        for (upc, items) in albumsByUPC where !matchedUPCs.contains(upc) {
            for item in items { discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .notInAppleMusic)) }
        }

        return LibraryImport(resolved: resolved, discarded: discarded, matches: matches)
    }

import CatalogKit
import FamilyStore
import Foundation
import PolicyEngine

/// The admin's unfiltered shelf — a denied favorite is a row here, no tile there.
public struct ReviewedLibrary: Sendable {
    public let favorites: [Annotated<FavoriteRow>]
    public let playlists: [ReviewedPlaylist]

    /// One entry per configured provider; failed and sparse look identical here.
    public let providers: [LibraryProviderID: ProviderHealth]

    /// Stored rows the catalog wouldn't resolve — delisted, or the request failed.
    public let unresolved: Int

    /// False when the catalog didn't answer; the screen says so once, not per row.
    public let isResolved: Bool

    public init(
        favorites: [Annotated<FavoriteRow>],
        playlists: [ReviewedPlaylist],
        providers: [LibraryProviderID: ProviderHealth],
        unresolved: Int,
        isResolved: Bool
    ) {
        self.favorites = favorites
        self.playlists = playlists
        self.providers = providers
        self.unresolved = unresolved
        self.isResolved = isResolved
    }

    /// Favorites the kid could not play today. What a parent came to see.
    public var blockedFavorites: [Annotated<FavoriteRow>] {
        favorites.filter { $0.isAllowedNow == false }
    }

    /// Favorites that arrived with the account, not chosen by the kid.
    public var adopted: [Annotated<FavoriteRow>] {
        favorites.filter { $0.fact.origin == .appleLibrary }
    }
}

public struct ReviewedPlaylist: Sendable, Identifiable {
    public let row: PlaylistRow
    public let entries: [Annotated<PlaylistEntryRow>]

    public var id: UUID { row.handle.local }

    /// Free text a child typed; a parent first reads it here.
    public var name: String { row.name }

    /// True when our copy takes an edit Apple's silently won't — a permanent gap.
    public var divergesFromApple: Bool {
        row.handle.appleLibraryID != nil && !row.appleIsOurs
    }

    public var blockedCount: Int { entries.filter { $0.isAllowedNow == false }.count }

    public init(row: PlaylistRow, entries: [Annotated<PlaylistEntryRow>]) {
        self.row = row
        self.entries = entries
    }
}

/// What one provider contributed to a read.
public enum ProviderHealth: Sendable, Hashable {
    case live

    /// Deliberately unused — not a fault, an answer given, or unasked.
    case notConfigured(Reason)

    /// Threw here; the kid's side swallows it, so one dead provider stays hidden.
    case failed(String)

    public enum Reason: Sendable, Hashable {
        /// `isSharedDevice`: the library signed in here is a grown-up's.
        case sharedDevice

        /// Onboarding hasn't asked, so nothing reads from an adult's library.
        case notYetAsked
    }
}

extension DeviceLibraryState {
    /// The pair of answers for isSharedDevice — false means neither is true.
    static func asked(shared: Bool) -> DeviceLibraryState {
        DeviceLibraryState(
            sharesDeviceWithChild: shared,
            childHasOwnAccount: !shared,
            hasBeenAsked: true
        )
    }
}

// MARK: - Wiring one up

@MainActor
struct Harness {
    let container: ModelContainer
    let context: ModelContext
    let kid: Kid
    let catalog = StubCatalog()
    let device: InMemoryDeviceLibraryState
    let cloudKit: CloudKitLibraryProvider
    private let providers: [any LibraryProvider]
    private(set) var library: MergedLibrary

    init(
        mode: SandboxMode = .denyPlusAuto,
        unrated: UnratedBehavior = .block,
        entries: [PolicyEntry] = [],
        extra: [any LibraryProvider] = [],
        device state: DeviceLibraryState = .asked(shared: false),
        container: ModelContainer? = nil
    ) throws {
        self.container = try container ?? FamilyStore.inMemoryContainer()
        context = ModelContext(self.container)

        if let existing = try context.fetch(FetchDescriptor<Kid>()).first {
            kid = existing
        } else {
            let family = Family(at: Fix.t0)
            let newKid = Kid(name: "Robin", mode: mode, unratedBehavior: unrated, at: Fix.t0)
            context.insert(family)
            context.insert(newKid)
            family.addKid(newKid, at: Fix.t0)
            kid = newKid
        }

        for entry in entries {
            kid.addEntry(kind: entry.kind, id: entry.id, displayName: entry.id.rawValue, at: Fix.t0)
        }
        try context.save()

        device = InMemoryDeviceLibraryState(state)
        cloudKit = CloudKitLibraryProvider(kid: kid, context: context)
        providers = [cloudKit] + extra
        library = MergedLibrary(
            providers: providers,
            catalog: catalog,
            engine: kid.makeEngine(),
            device: device
        )
    }

    /// Rebuilds against the kid's current policy — what a parent's edit triggers.
    mutating func repolicy(_ change: (Kid) -> Void) throws {
        change(kid)
        try context.save()
        library = MergedLibrary(
            providers: providers,
            catalog: catalog,
            engine: kid.makeEngine(),
            device: device
        )
    }
}

        #expect(reviewed.providers[.appleMusic] == .notConfigured(.notYetAsked))

    @Test("A provider that throws is reported to the parent")
    func failureIsReported() async throws {
        let provider = StubProvider()
        provider.isFailing = true
        let harness = try Harness(extra: [provider])

        let reviewed = await harness.library.reviewed()
        guard case .failed = reviewed.providers[.appleMusic] else {
            Issue.record("expected a failure, got \(String(describing: reviewed.providers[.appleMusic]))")
            return
        }
        // And it did not empty the shelf.
        #expect(reviewed.providers[.cloudKit] == .live)
    }

A library read keeps each row's handle, its date, and its page

The seeding flow only ever wanted one page of the library and a flat list of
catalog matches, so `resolveToCatalog` returned `resolved` alone and collapsed
two library rows sharing an ISRC onto one. A shelf that reads the library
needs the other half: which library row became which catalog item, when the
account added it, and the next page after this one.

Three additive changes, all defaulted so the seeding flow and its stub are
untouched: `LibraryItem` carries `addedAt` and `albumTitle`, `LibraryImport`
carries `matches` keyed by library id, and `libraryItems` takes an `offset`,
sorted newest-first so a capped read keeps what was added last. The match
runs back from the response's own ISRC/UPC because the catalog item carries
no code, and the per-code buckets are arrays now so both rows of a duplicated
recording get their match.

`Song.libraryAddedDate`, `Song.albumTitle`, `MusicLibraryRequest.offset` and
`sort(by:ascending:)` all compile against the iOS SDK at the iOS 17 floor;
none has run against a real account yet.

import Foundation

/// Who is at the screen; with the device answers, the whole of which providers open.
public enum LibraryAudience: Sendable, Hashable {
    /// The kid: our store always, the Apple library only if it's their own.
    case kid

    /// A grown-up behind the passcode: the Apple library alone, walls down.
    case grownUp
}

/// One table for the gate and the admin's health line, so they can't disagree.
public enum LibraryLiveness: Sendable, Hashable {
    /// Read from and, capability permitting, written to.
    case live

    /// Written to but not yet read from — onboarding hasn't asked.
    case notReadable(ProviderHealth.Reason)

    /// Neither, and the reason is an answer someone gave, not a fault.
    case notLive(ProviderHealth.Reason)

    public var isLive: Bool {
        if case .notLive = self { return false }
        return true
    }

    public var isReadable: Bool { self == .live }

    public static func status(
        of id: LibraryProviderID,
        device: DeviceLibraryState,
        audience: LibraryAudience
    ) -> LibraryLiveness {
        switch (audience, id) {
        // A grown-up's shelf is their library and nothing of the kid's, whatever
        // the device answers say: the answers describe whose library this is,
        // and the grown-up just said it's theirs by unlocking.
        case (.grownUp, .appleMusic): .live
        case (.grownUp, .cloudKit): .notLive(.grownUpMode)

        case (.kid, .cloudKit): .live
        case (.kid, .appleMusic):
            if device.isSharedDevice {
                .notLive(.sharedDevice)
            } else if !device.hasBeenAsked {
                .notReadable(.notYetAsked)
            } else {
                .live
            }
        }
    }
}

    nonisolated let capabilities: LibraryCapabilities

    var isFailing = false

    private(set) var playlistRows: [PlaylistRow] = []

import CatalogKit
import CryptoKit
import FamilyStore
import Foundation
import PolicyEngine

/// Why the Apple library contributed nothing; anything else is passed through.
public enum AppleLibraryUnavailable: Error, Hashable, Sendable {
    /// iCloud Music Library is off for this account — a setting, not a fault.
    case cloudLibraryOff
}

/// How much of a library one read takes. Constants until a real one is measured.
public struct AppleLibraryLimits: Sendable, Hashable {
    /// Per request; the ISRC and UPC lookups cap at 300 and 100 identifiers.
    public var songPage = 300
    public var albumPage = 100

    /// Newest first, so the cap keeps what the account added last.
    public var songs = 500
    public var albums = 200

    /// How long a snapshot is served before a read is started behind it.
    public var freshFor: TimeInterval = 10 * 60

    /// How soon a failed read is tried again — not the full ten minutes.
    public var retryAfter: TimeInterval = 60

    public init() {}
}

/// What the last completed read found; the admin's numbers.
public struct AppleLibraryRead: Sendable, Hashable {
    public let at: Date
    public let songs: Int
    public let albums: Int

    /// Library rows with no catalog match — research question 2, measured.
    public let unresolved: Int
}

/// The account's own library, read and never written; live only if it's the kid's.
///
/// A snapshot, not a query: `favorites()` is on the home screen's critical
/// path and runs on every heart tap, so it returns what the last read found
/// and starts the next read behind it when that's gone stale. The app awaits
/// `refresh()` on launch and foreground and reloads the shelf after.
///
/// Nothing here is stored. A row lives exactly as long as the account keeps
/// the item, and the shelf empties if the library becomes unreadable.
@MainActor
public final class AppleMusicLibraryProvider: LibraryProvider {
    public nonisolated let id = LibraryProviderID.appleMusic

    /// Read-only, so every write path in the merge sits this provider out.
    public nonisolated let capabilities: LibraryCapabilities = []

    private let source: any LibrarySource
    private let access: any CatalogAccess
    private let cache: (any ItemCache)?
    private let limits: AppleLibraryLimits
    private let now: @Sendable () -> Date

    private var favoriteRows: [FavoriteRow] = []
    private var playlistRows: [PlaylistRow] = []

    /// Lineage the merge named after the fact, kept so it's named once.
    private var learned: [CatalogID: LibraryAncestry] = [:]

    private var refreshing: Task<Void, any Error>?
    private var attemptedAt: Date?

    /// The last read that finished; nil until one has.
    public private(set) var lastRead: AppleLibraryRead?

    /// Why the last attempt failed; nil once one succeeds.
    public private(set) var lastFailure: (any Error)?

    /// - Parameter cache: where matched items go, so the shelf's own lookup
    ///   finds them warm instead of paying a request per page of rows.
    public init(
        source: any LibrarySource,
        access: any CatalogAccess,
        cache: (any ItemCache)? = nil,
        limits: AppleLibraryLimits = AppleLibraryLimits(),
        now: @escaping @Sendable () -> Date = { Date() }
    ) {
        self.source = source
        self.access = access
        self.cache = cache
        self.limits = limits
        self.now = now
    }

    // MARK: - Reading

    /// The snapshot; throws only when there's nothing to serve and a reason why.
    public func favorites() async throws -> [FavoriteRow] {
        try serve()
        return favoriteRows
    }

    public func playlists() async throws -> [PlaylistRow] {
        try serve()
        return playlistRows
    }

    private func serve() throws {
        refreshIfStale()
        if lastRead == nil, let failure = lastFailure { throw failure }
    }

    /// Reads now, once; a read already running is joined rather than doubled.
    public func refresh() async throws {
        try await startRefresh().value
    }

    private var isStale: Bool {
        guard let attemptedAt else { return true }
        let age = now().timeIntervalSince(attemptedAt)
        return age > (lastFailure == nil ? limits.freshFor : limits.retryAfter)
    }

    private func refreshIfStale() {
        guard isStale else { return }
        _ = startRefresh()
    }

    private func startRefresh() -> Task<Void, any Error> {
        if let refreshing { return refreshing }
        attemptedAt = now()
        let task = Task { [weak self] in
            guard let self else { return }
            defer { self.refreshing = nil }
            try await self.read()
        }
        refreshing = task
        return task
    }

    private func read() async throws {
        do {
            let state = try await access.subscriptionState()
            guard state.hasCloudLibraryEnabled else { throw AppleLibraryUnavailable.cloudLibraryOff }

            let songs = try await read(.song, page: limits.songPage, cap: limits.songs)
            let albums = try await read(.album, page: limits.albumPage, cap: limits.albums)

            favoriteRows = (songs.rows + albums.rows).sorted { $0.favoritedAt > $1.favoritedAt }
            lastRead = AppleLibraryRead(
                at: now(),
                songs: songs.rows.count,
                albums: albums.rows.count,
                unresolved: songs.unresolved + albums.unresolved
            )
            lastFailure = nil
        } catch {
            lastFailure = error
            throw error
        }
    }

    /// Pages by offset up to the cap; a short page is the end of the library.
    private func read(
        _ kind: ItemKind,
        page: Int,
        cap: Int
    ) async throws -> (rows: [FavoriteRow], unresolved: Int) {
        var rows: [FavoriteRow] = []
        var unresolved = 0
        var offset = 0
        while offset < cap {
            let wanted = min(page, cap - offset)
            let items = try await source.libraryItems(kinds: [kind], limit: wanted, offset: offset)
            guard !items.isEmpty else { break }

            let matched = try await source.resolveToCatalog(items)
            await cache?.store(Array(matched.matches.values))
            for item in items {
                guard let match = matched.matches[item.id] else {
                    unresolved += 1
                    continue
                }
                rows.append(row(for: item, matching: match))
            }

            if items.count < wanted { break }
            offset += items.count
        }
        return (rows, unresolved)
    }

    private func row(for item: LibraryItem, matching match: CatalogItem) -> FavoriteRow {
        FavoriteRow(
            id: Self.stableID(for: item.id),
            catalogID: match.id,
            displayName: match.title,
            artworkURL: match.artworkURL ?? item.artworkURL,
            favoritedAt: item.addedAt ?? .distantPast,
            origin: .appleLibrary,
            ancestry: learned[match.id] ?? Self.ancestry(of: match, named: item)
        )
    }

    /// Ids from the match, names from the library side — no request to name them.
    ///
    /// Filled here so the merge's top-up, which names only rows with *no*
    /// lineage, leaves these alone: five hundred rows would otherwise be named
    /// again on every read of the browser. Empty ids are dropped, as everywhere.
    private static func ancestry(of match: CatalogItem, named item: LibraryItem) -> LibraryAncestry {
        var out = LibraryAncestry()
        for ancestor in match.ancestors where !ancestor.id.rawValue.isEmpty {
            switch ancestor.id.kind {
            case .album where out.albumID == nil:
                out.albumID = ancestor.id.rawValue
                out.albumName = item.albumTitle
            case .artist where out.artistID == nil:
                out.artistID = ancestor.id.rawValue
                out.artistName = item.subtitle
            default:
                break
            }
        }
        return out
    }

    /// The same library row is the same row on every read — and never stored.
    nonisolated static func stableID(for libraryID: String) -> UUID {
        let digest = SHA256.hash(data: Data("appleLibrary:\(libraryID)".utf8))
        var bytes = Array(digest.prefix(16))
        // Version and variant bits, so it reads as a name-based UUID.
        bytes[6] = (bytes[6] & 0x0F) | 0x50
        bytes[8] = (bytes[8] & 0x3F) | 0x80
        return bytes.withUnsafeBufferPointer { NSUUID(uuidBytes: $0.baseAddress!) as UUID }
    }

    // MARK: - What the merge tells us

    /// Kept in memory only, on the rows and for the next read to reuse.
    public func recordAncestry(_ ancestry: [CatalogID: LibraryAncestry]) async throws {
        guard !ancestry.isEmpty else { return }
        learned.merge(ancestry) { _, new in new }
        favoriteRows = favoriteRows.map { row in
            guard let found = ancestry[row.catalogID] else { return row }
            return FavoriteRow(
                id: row.id,
                catalogID: row.catalogID,
                displayName: row.displayName,
                artworkURL: row.artworkURL,
                favoritedAt: row.favoritedAt,
                origin: row.origin,
                ancestry: found
            )
        }
    }

    // MARK: - Writes: none

    public func addFavorite(
        _ id: CatalogID,
        displayName: String,
        artworkURL: URL?,
        origin: LibraryOrigin,
        ancestry: LibraryAncestry
    ) async throws {}

    public func removeFavorite(_ id: CatalogID) async throws {}

    public func createPlaylist(named name: String, songs: [LibrarySong]) async throws -> PlaylistRow {
        throw LibraryUnavailable()
    }

    public func addToPlaylist(_ handle: PlaylistHandle, song: LibrarySong) async throws {}
    public func removeFromPlaylist(_ handle: PlaylistHandle, song: CatalogID) async throws {}
    public func reorderPlaylist(_ handle: PlaylistHandle, to order: [CatalogID]) async throws {}
    public func renamePlaylist(_ handle: PlaylistHandle, to name: String) async throws {}
    public func deletePlaylist(_ handle: PlaylistHandle) async throws {}
}

actor StubLibrarySource: LibrarySource {

        self.catalogMatches = catalogMatches
    }

    func libraryItems(kinds: Set<ItemKind>, limit: Int, offset: Int) async throws -> [LibraryItem] {
        for kind in kinds { pages.append((kind, limit, offset)) }
        return Array(library.filter { kinds.contains($0.kind) }.dropFirst(offset).prefix(limit))
    }

    func searchLibrary(term: String, kinds: Set<ItemKind>, limit: Int) async throws -> [LibraryItem] {
        []
    }

    func resolveToCatalog(_ items: [LibraryItem]) async throws -> LibraryImport {
        resolveCallCount += 1
        var resolved: [CatalogItem] = []
        var discarded: [DiscardedItem] = []
        var matches: [String: CatalogItem] = [:]
        for item in items {
            guard let code = item.isrc ?? item.upc else {
                discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .noIdentifier))
                continue
            }
            if let match = catalogMatches[code] {
                if !resolved.contains(where: { $0.id == match.id }) { resolved.append(match) }
                matches[item.id] = match
            } else {
                discarded.append(DiscardedItem(item: item, reason: .notInAppleMusic))
            }
        }
        return LibraryImport(resolved: resolved, discarded: discarded, matches: matches)
    }
}

/// Authorization and subscription as a test says they are.
final class StubAccess: CatalogAccess, @unchecked Sendable {
    var hasCloudLibrary = true

    init(hasCloudLibrary: Bool = true) {
        self.hasCloudLibrary = hasCloudLibrary
    }

    func requestAuthorization() async -> AuthorizationStatus { .authorized }

    var authorizationStatus: AuthorizationStatus { .authorized }

    func subscriptionState() async throws -> SubscriptionState {
        SubscriptionState(
            canPlayCatalogContent: true,
            canBecomeSubscriber: false,
            hasCloudLibraryEnabled: hasCloudLibrary
        )
    }

    var subscriptionUpdates: AsyncStream<SubscriptionState> { AsyncStream { $0.finish() } }
}

album title and artist name — so the top-up that names unnamed rows leaves

land, so the shelf's own lookup finds them warm.

vote on; the browser derives them from song lineage, which is what it does

    // MARK: - Apple Music access

    /// Settles authorization, then lets the subscription answer arrive behind
    /// the app rather than in front of it.
    ///
    /// **Authorization is awaited and the subscription is not**, because they
    /// cost nothing alike. Authorization is answered locally in single-digit
    /// milliseconds and decides whether this app can do its job at all. The
    /// subscription is a network round trip to Apple that takes as long as it
    /// takes — measured hanging indefinitely in the simulator — and the whole
    /// app used to sit behind it under a spinner. That is the launch cost:
    /// nothing was wrong, we were waiting for a question whose answer is yes
    /// for every real user of this app.
    ///
    /// So it is assumed yes and checked afterwards. The optimism gives away
    /// nothing: an account that cannot play catalog content still cannot, and
    /// the screen swaps to ``Access/cannotPlay(_:)`` the moment the answer says
    /// so — before a kid can get much further than looking at their shelves,
    /// and nothing they tap in the meantime will produce sound it should not.
    ///
    /// **A failure to reach Apple is not a negative answer**, which is why the
    /// error is dropped rather than shown. Only a definite "this account cannot
    /// play" takes the app down. An offline device leaves the app up and lets
    /// playback fail with its own error, which names the real problem —
    /// ``CatalogError/offline`` — instead of telling a parent their
    /// subscription is the trouble when it is not.
    func start() async {
        let status = await musicAccess.requestAuthorization()
        guard status == .authorized else {
            access = .needsAuthorization(status)
            return
        }

        access = .ready

        guard let subscription = try? await musicAccess.subscriptionState() else { return }
        hasCloudLibrary = subscription.hasCloudLibraryEnabled
        guard !subscription.canPlayCatalogContent else { return }
        access = .cannotPlay(subscription)
    }

    /// tab and lets the read fail with its own error rather than telling a

    private(set) var hasCloudLibrary: Bool?

    /// Rebuilds everything that holds a policy engine, and re-reads what it
    /// judged. What a parent's edit turns into.
    private func rebuildCatalog() {
        rebuildEngines()
        reloadLibraryContents()
    }

    /// Re-indexes the policy into the three things that hold one.
    ///
    /// All three, always. A policy edit that reached the catalog but not the
    /// library would leave a denied artist off search results and still on the
    /// kid's shelf — the one screen a parent is least likely to check.
    ///
    /// Split out from ``rebuildCatalog()`` because this half is cheap and the
    /// other half is not, and one caller needs only this: a kid dismissing a
    /// suggestion changes what they may reach and must take effect at once, but
    /// blanking the library browser under them because they tapped "no thanks"
    /// on the home screen would be the app flinching at its own bookkeeping.
    private func rebuildEngines() {
        // Whatever is being walked belongs to the kid and the policy that were
        // current when it started. A walk writes through a provider holding a
        // `Kid`, so one left running past a kid switch would keep filing one
        // child's artist into whichever library is open now.
        cancelWalks()
        let engine = kid.makeEngine()
        self.engine = engine
        policyGeneration += 1
        catalog = FilteredCatalog(source: source, engine: engine)
        library = MergedLibrary(
            providers: [CloudKitLibraryProvider(kid: kid, context: context)],
            catalog: source,
            engine: engine,
            device: deviceLibraryStore
        )
    }

    /// Drops what the previous engine judged and reads it again.

        // left to refresh: it was judged by the engine that just stopped being
        // the policy, and every column and drill-in below it is a filter of that
        // one value. A parent denying an artist with the library open would
        // otherwise leave them sitting there, on the one screen a kid is most
        // likely to be looking at.
        let wasBrowsing = hasLoadedLibrary
        libraryContents = .empty
        hasLoadedLibrary = false
        Task {
            await refreshLibrary()
            // Only for a screen that already had it. Reading it for a kid who
            // has never opened the library would spend a request on a screen
            // nobody is looking at.
            if wasBrowsing { await loadLibrary() }
        }
    }

        // **A link can arrive while the app is already running**, straight from

        .onChange(of: shares.waiting.count) { _, count in

        // Coming back is when a co-parent's edits are most likely to be waiting,
        // and when this device's own are most likely to be owed. Nothing fires on
        // the way in — `onChange` skips the initial value — so this does not
        // double up with the `task` above.
        .onChange(of: scenePhase) { _, phase in
            guard phase == .active else { return }
            Task { await session.syncPass() }
        }

    /// waits on this. **Gated on the same table the merge reads**, because the
    /// provider itself doesn't know whose library it is looking at: on a shared

        try? await appleLibrary.refresh()

A kid's own Apple Music library reaches their shelf

The provider joins the kid's list at both build sites and in the admin's
review, and the existing gate decides the rest: on a device whose answers
say the library is the kid's own it is read, and on a shared device it is
not, exactly as the stub tests have asserted since the seam went in.

The read runs behind the app — on launch, on foreground, and the moment the
onboarding answer makes the library the kid's — and the shelf reloads after,
so nothing on the kid's side waits on it. It is gated on the same table the
merge reads rather than left to the merge alone, because the provider does
not know whose library it is looking at: on a shared device a grown-up's
library must not be read into memory at all, drawn or not.

The onboarding and admin copy promised that favorites would be written to
the child's Apple Music library. That is the writing stage, which has not
shipped; the sentences now describe what this build does.

    /// the answer travels with what is being written rather than with the app's

    /// Plays one item, with the rest of its surface behind it.
    ///

    /// the shelf — whatever list the tap came from is the queue, and the tapped

    /// The two are handed over separately and nothing guarantees they agree —

    /// the entry alone rather than dropping it — playback asks again anyway, and
    /// an offline launch that emptied the bar would look like the queue was lost.
    ///
    /// **Nothing is logged.** A blocked entry here is a stored row that is still
    /// on disk, the same shape as a blocked favorite, so the report can find it
    /// whenever it is asked; writing a block on every launch would drown the
    /// parent's report in one kid's Tuesday.
    func revalidate() async {
        guard !queue.isEmpty, status == .stopped, !hasStartedCurrent else { return }

        var allowed: [Entry] = []
        for entry in queue {
            guard let verdict = try? await session.catalog.verdict(for: entry.item) else {
                allowed.append(entry)
                continue
            }
            if verdict.isAllowed { allowed.append(entry) }

        guard allowed.count != queue.count else { return }

        index = allowed.firstIndex { $0.item.id == wasCurrent } ?? 0

+
        cancelWalks()
        // **The one builder, and it asks who is looking.** Every policy edit,
        // kid switch, dismissal and sync-driven clear comes through here, and
        // one that rebuilt for the kid while a grown-up was listening would put
        // the walls back up under a band still saying they are down.
        let engine: PolicyEngine
        let providers: [any LibraryProvider]
        switch audience {
        case .kid:
            engine = kid.makeEngine()
            providers = [CloudKitLibraryProvider(kid: kid, context: context), appleLibrary]
        case .grownUp:
            // Level 3 with no entries allows everything before a rating is ever
            // looked at, so `unratedBehavior` is never consulted here.
            engine = PolicyEngine(policy: Policy(mode: .reportOnly))
            providers = [appleLibrary]
        }
        self.engine = engine
        policyGeneration += 1
        catalog = FilteredCatalog(source: source, engine: engine)
        library = MergedLibrary(
            providers: providers,
            catalog: source,
            engine: engine,
            device: deviceLibraryStore,
            audience: audience
        )
    }

    /// A grown-up takes the player, or gives it back.
    ///
    /// Not ``switchedKid()``, though it looks like one: that saves the outgoing
    /// queue under its owner and restores the incoming owner's, and a grown-up
    /// has no slot. Reused, it would put the kid's queue on the grown-up's bar
    /// on the way in and write the grown-up's queue into the kid's slot on the
    /// way out. Here the kid's queue is saved on the way in and restored on the
    /// way out, and the grown-up's is simply dropped.
    ///
    /// Called by the screen when ``Session/audience`` changes, either way.
    func audienceChanged() async {
        await clearForAudienceChange()
        owner = currentOwner
        restore()
    }

    /// The way out, from the band's button.
    ///
    /// The queue is cleared **before** the session rebuilds the kid's engine,
    /// because that rebuild triggers ``revalidatePlaying()``, which would find
    /// the grown-up's track at `index`, judge it under the kid's policy, and
    /// write a block in the kid's name for a song the kid never heard.
    func leaveGrownUpMode() async {
        await clearForAudienceChange()
        await session.leaveGrownUpMode()
    }

    private func clearForAudienceChange() async {
        watchdog?.cancel()
        watchdog = nil
        // The kid's, under their name; a no-op for a grown-up's, which has none.
        save()
        enqueued = nil
        await session.stop()
        owner = nil
        queue = []
        index = 0
        status = .stopped
        message = nil
        resetTrackState()
    }

A grown-up can take the player, and nothing they do is written

Grown-up mode: on a shared device, behind the passcode, the player reads the
grown-up's own Apple Music library and nothing of the kid's, judges against
an engine that allows everything, and writes nothing — not a play, a search,
a block, or a visit, and the Recent shelf and the parent's suggestion shelves
answer empty. It ends only by the button; a parent listening with the screen
off is the case it exists for, and the band that says it's on is what the
next kid to pick the device up will see.

`rebuildEngines()` is now the one builder and asks who is looking. It runs
on every policy edit, kid switch, dismissal and sync-driven clear, and one
that rebuilt for the kid while a grown-up was listening would have put the
walls back up under a band still saying they are down.

The player's queue owner became optional for a reason the kid switch already
records: `switchedKid()` saves the outgoing queue under its owner and restores
the incoming one, and a grown-up has no slot. Reused for the mode change it
would have put the kid's queue on the grown-up's bar going in and written the
grown-up's queue into the kid's slot coming out. Leaving clears the queue
*before* the session rebuilds the kid's engine, because that rebuild
re-judges what is at `index`, and the grown-up's track judged under the
kid's policy would be a block written in the kid's name for a song they
never heard.

git add Apps/AuralSandbox/AuralSandbox/Session.swift Apps/AuralSandbox/AuralSandbox/KidPlayerModel.swift Apps/AuralSandbox/AuralSandbox/KidHomeView.swift && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
A grown-up can take the player, and nothing they do is written

Grown-up mode: on a shared device, behind the passcode, the player reads the
grown-up's own Apple Music library and nothing of the kid's, judges against
an engine that allows everything, and writes nothing — not a play, a search,
a block, or a visit, and the Recent shelf and the parent's suggestion shelves
answer empty. It ends only by the button; a parent listening with the screen
off is the case it exists for, and the band that says it's on is what the
next kid to pick the device up will see.

`rebuildEngines()` is now the one builder and asks who is looking. It runs
on every policy edit, kid switch, dismissal and sync-driven clear, and one
that rebuilt for the kid while a grown-up was listening would have put the
walls back up under a band still saying they are down.

The player's queue owner became optional for a reason the kid switch already
records: `switchedKid()` saves the outgoing queue under its owner and restores
the incoming one, and a grown-up has no slot. Reused for the mode change it
would have put the kid's queue on the grown-up's bar going in and written the
grown-up's queue into the kid's slot coming out. Leaving clears the queue
*before* the session rebuilds the kid's engine, because that rebuild
re-judges what is at `index`, and the grown-up's track judged under the
kid's policy would be a block written in the kid's name for a song they
never heard.

---- LibraryControls 1-150
import CatalogKit
import FamilyStore
import KidLibrary
import SwiftUI

/// The heart.
///
/// Filled and outline, no count, no animation a kid has to sit through. It reads
/// the same on a song, an album and an artist even though the primitive
/// underneath differs by kind — that difference is the seam's problem and never
/// the kid's.
///
/// **Never drawn on the artwork.** The standing rule is clipping yes,
/// compositing never, and a heart burned onto Apple's pixels is exactly what
/// that forbids. So it sits in the text area of a tile and beside the play
/// button on a row.
struct HeartButton: View {
    @Bindable var session: Session
    let item: CatalogItem
    let origin: PlaybackOrigin

    /// Big enough for a finger that is not very accurate yet, without pushing
    /// the title it sits beside off the line.
    static let size: CGFloat = 28

    private var isOn: Bool { session.isFavorite(item.id) }

    var body: some View {
        Button {
            // The failure message is discarded on purpose, and the heart is
            // still honest: it draws from rows re-read after the write, so a
            // write that did not land leaves it exactly as it was. Nothing about
            // a store failing is a thing to put in front of a six-year-old.
            Task { _ = await session.toggleFavorite(item, origin: origin) }
        } label: {
            Image(systemName: isOn ? "heart.fill" : "heart")
                .font(.body.weight(.semibold))
                .foregroundStyle(isOn ? AnyShapeStyle(.tint) : AnyShapeStyle(.secondary))
                // **`symbolEffect`, not `contentTransition`, and the difference
                // matters.** `BounceSymbolEffect` conforms to
                // `DiscreteSymbolEffect`, so this overload watches `value`
                // itself and needs no animation in the transaction — unlike the
                // play/pause replace in ``NowPlayingBar``, which does.
                //
                // The one place in the app overshoot is the content rather than
                // the motion: this is the only tap a kid makes that means
                // *mine*, and it is worth a reply.
                .symbolEffect(.bounce, value: isOn)
                .frame(width: Self.size, height: Self.size)
                .contentShape(Rectangle())
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(isOn ? "Remove from your library" : "Add to your library")
    }
}

/// The same heart, with its name beside it.
///
/// A glyph is enough on a row or a tile, where it sits next to the title it
/// belongs to and every row has one. At the top of an artist's page there is no
/// column of hearts to read it against and nothing next to it to belong to, so
/// the word does the work the pattern usually does — and the tap target stops
/// being 28 points of empty header.
///
/// Same call, same silence on failure, same rule about never touching the
/// artwork: it sits under the picture, not on it.
struct FavoriteButton: View {
    @Bindable var session: Session
    let item: CatalogItem
    let origin: PlaybackOrigin

    private var isOn: Bool { session.isFavorite(item.id) }

    var body: some View {
        Button {
            Task { _ = await session.toggleFavorite(item, origin: origin) }
        } label: {
            Label(isOn ? "In your library" : "Add to your library",
                  systemImage: isOn ? "heart.fill" : "heart")
                .font(.headline)
                .padding(.horizontal, 20)
                .padding(.vertical, 12)
                .contentShape(Capsule())
        }
        .buttonStyle(.pressable)
        .foregroundStyle(isOn ? AnyShapeStyle(.tint) : AnyShapeStyle(.primary))
        .background(Capsule().fill(.quaternary))
        // The label already says which state it is in, so a hint would be the
        // same sentence twice.
        .accessibilityLabel(isOn ? "Remove from your library" : "Add to your library")
    }
}

/// Put this song on a playlist.
///
/// A menu of the kid's playlists plus one way to make another, which is what
/// makes "songs are added from anywhere a song appears" true without a screen
/// per gesture. Absent when there is nothing to add — a menu whose only entry is
/// "new" is a button wearing a menu's clothes, so that case is a button.
struct AddToPlaylistButton: View {
    @Bindable var session: Session
    let item: CatalogItem
    let origin: PlaybackOrigin

    @State private var isNaming = false

    var body: some View {
        Group {
            if session.playlists.isEmpty {
                Button { isNaming = true } label: { glyph }
                    .buttonStyle(.plain)
            } else {
                Menu {
                    ForEach(session.playlists) { playlist in
                        Button(playlist.name) { add(to: playlist.handle) }
                    }
                    Divider()
                    Button("New playlist…") { isNaming = true }
                } label: {
                    glyph
                }
                .menuStyle(.borderlessButton)
                .menuIndicator(.hidden)
                .fixedSize()
            }
        }
        .accessibilityLabel("Add to a playlist")
        .sheet(isPresented: $isNaming) {
            NamePlaylistSheet(session: session, songs: [item])
        }
    }

    private var glyph: some View {
        Image(systemName: "text.badge.plus")
            .font(.body.weight(.semibold))
            .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            .frame(width: HeartButton.size, height: HeartButton.size)
            .contentShape(Rectangle())
    }

    private func add(to handle: PlaylistHandle) {
        Task { _ = await session.addToPlaylist(handle, song: item, origin: origin) }
    }
}

/// Naming a playlist. A keyboard and one field.
///
/// The name is free text a child typed. It reaches their Apple Music library and
/// the parent's report, which is worth knowing about the field rather than
/// discovering later.

                if item.id.kind == .song {
                    Button { onPlay(item) } label: { Tile(item: item, hasHeart: true) }
                } else {

        // Outside the tap target's label, for the same reason the heart is: a
        // button inside another button's label is dead. An overlay rather than a
        // third child of the `ZStack` above, because reaching the far corner
        // from a `.bottomLeading` stack means a child that fills the frame, and

        //

        .overlay(alignment: .topTrailing) {

        .contextMenu {
            if item.id.kind == .song {
                PlaylistMenuItems(session: session, item: item, origin: origin)
            }
            if let onDismiss {
                Button("No thanks", systemImage: "xmark", role: .destructive, action: onDismiss)
            }
        }
    }
}

/// "No thanks" on a suggested tile.
///
/// Drawn over the artwork's top corner rather than beside the title, because the
/// title line is already carrying a kind glyph and a heart's worth of reserved
/// space. Over artwork it needs its own backing to stay visible on a bright
/// album cover — a bare glyph disappears against half the catalog.
///
/// **Nothing is clipped or composited into the artwork.** This sits above it in
/// the stack, the way the heart does; the pixels underneath are untouched, which
/// is the same reading of License §3.3.6(D) the rest of the app works to.
struct DismissButton: View {
    let action: () -> Void

    var body: some View {
        Button(action: action) {
            Image(systemName: "xmark")
                .font(.caption.weight(.bold))
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .frame(width: HeartButton.size, height: HeartButton.size)
                .background(Circle().fill(.black.opacity(0.45)))
                .contentShape(Circle())
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel("No thanks")
        .accessibilityHint("Takes this off your shelf")
    }
}

/// The add-to-playlist half of a context menu, so a song reached as a tile has
/// the same reach as one reached as a row.
struct PlaylistMenuItems: View {
    @Bindable var session: Session
    let item: CatalogItem
    let origin: PlaybackOrigin

    var body: some View {
        ForEach(session.playlists) { playlist in
            Button("Add to \(playlist.name)") {
                Task { _ = await session.addToPlaylist(playlist.handle, song: item, origin: origin) }
            }
        }
    }
}

---- STYLE.md 420-470

### 3.3 Colour and identity

The app has no colour. `Assets.xcassets` contains only `AppIcon.appiconset`.

**Ship three colour sets, not one.** The split is forced by arithmetic, not
taste: a colour that reads *as* text on a dark background needs relative
luminance ≥ 0.276; a colour that carries a white label *behind* it needs ≤ 0.183.
No single value satisfies both, so one `AccentColor` used for both roles silently
fails contrast in dark mode.

| Set | Role | Call sites |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KidAccent` | foreground tint | the `.tint` / `.foregroundStyle(.tint)` sites |
| `KidAccentFill` | background of primary actions | `.borderedProminent` at `AlbumView.swift:63`, `ArtistView.swift:102`, `KidHomeView.swift:478` |
| `AdminAccent` | the grown-up half | `.tint(.adminAccent)` on the admin sheet, `KidHomeView.swift:223` |

Each colour set needs four entries: base, `luminosity: dark`, `contrast: high`,
and both. Set
`ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GLOBAL_ACCENT_COLOR_NAME = KidAccent` in **both** build
configurations (beside `ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME`). Do not create a set
literally named `AccentColor` — the setting takes a name.

**The generated symbol is `Color(.kidAccent)`, not `Color.kidAccent`.** An
earlier draft of this file said the latter and it does not compile.
`ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GENERATE_ASSET_SYMBOL_FRAMEWORKS = SwiftUI` generates
**only** `extension DeveloperToolsSupport.ColorResource { static let kidAccent }`
— there is no static member on `Color` and none on `ShapeStyle where Self ==
Color`, so a leading-dot `.kidAccent` in a `.tint(…)` fails to infer as well
(`.tint` is overloaded on `Color?` and `some ShapeStyle`). Use the
`Color(_:ColorResource)` initializer and it is unambiguous everywhere. Check
`GeneratedAssetSymbols.swift` in DerivedData if in doubt rather than guessing.

Per CLAUDE.md's warning about silently-ignored build settings: verify with
`plutil -p` on the built app and look for `NSAccentColorName` — never
`plutil -extract` without `-o -`. Confirmed present on 2026-08-03, along with all
three colour sets in `Assets.car` via `xcrun assetutil --info`.

**A fill colour is needed wherever the accent is a background under a white
label**, and `.borderedProminent` is exactly that — so those sites carry an
explicit `.tint(Color(.kidAccentFill))`. Note the asymmetry that makes this
necessary is *dark mode only*: contrast is symmetric, so a colour at 4.6:1
against white works both as text on white and as a background carrying white
text. It is the dark variants that diverge — a foreground tint has to be light to
read on a dark background, and a light fill cannot carry a white label. The same
trap applies to `swipeActions`, which is why `AdminView`'s "Rename" keeps
`.tint(.blue)`: it needs an `AdminAccentFill` that does not exist.

**Splitting kid and parent accents is deliberate.** The passcode gate is a mode
boundary and a parent should see at a glance which half they are in; the admin
sheet is a clean scope with no leakage; and the *kid* accent is the one the

---- NowPlayingBar head
import CatalogKit
import FamilyStore
import SwiftUI

/// What is playing, and the controls that go with it.
///
/// Play, pause, skip, and the heart. No shuffle, no repeat, no next-up list —
/// the bar itself stays as narrow as it ever was. Tapping the artwork or the
/// title opens ``NowPlayingView``, which is the same controls at a bigger size,
/// a scrubber, links to the record and the artist, and the way onto a playlist.
///
/// **What is not here is a space decision, not a policy one.** A phone gives
/// this row one line, and every glyph on it is a word of the title the kid
/// cannot read. So the title takes the room and the two things that survived
/// the cut are the ones a kid reaches for mid-song.
///
/// Skip stops at the end of the queue rather than finding something else to
/// play. Autoplay past the end is the fourth MusicKit affordance this app never
/// uses, and the queue living in ``KidPlayerModel`` is what makes that true by
/// construction rather than by remembering to switch it off.
struct NowPlayingBar: View {
    @Bindable var session: Session
    @Bindable var player: KidPlayerModel

    #if os(iOS)
    /// Shared with ``NowPlayingView``, because opening the player is one
    /// movement that starts here and ends there and a finger may turn back
    /// halfway through it.
    ///
    /// From the environment for the same reason ``KidRouter`` is. It used to be
    /// that eight screens drew this bar and threading a parameter through all of
    /// them was an initializer argument per screen forever; now ``KidHomeView``
    /// draws it once, beneath the whole stack, and the environment is what
    /// reaches *out* of the inset to the expansion held on the screen around it.
    /// Nil wherever nobody put one up, and the drag is simply absent there — the
    /// tap is not, because it never needed anything.
    @Environment(PlayerExpansion.self) private var expansion: PlayerExpansion?
    #else
    @State private var isExpanded = false
    #endif

// MARK: - Grown-up mode

/// The band that says a grown-up has the player, and the one way out.
///
/// The admin's colour, for the reason the admin sheet has it: the passcode is a
/// mode boundary and this is the other side of it, drawn on the kid's screens.
/// Tinted rather than filled — `AdminAccent` is a foreground colour and there
/// is no fill variant that would carry a white label in dark mode (see
/// STYLE.md §3.3), so it sits on the bar material like the bars beneath it.
///
/// No passcode to leave. Going back to the kid's side is the safe direction,
/// and anyone should be able to take it.
struct GrownUpBand: View {
    @Bindable var session: Session
    @Bindable var player: KidPlayerModel

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
            HStack {
                Label("Grown-up mode", systemImage: "person.fill")
                    .font(.headline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.tint)
                Spacer()
                Button("Back to kid mode") {
                    Task { await player.leaveGrownUpMode() }
                }
                .buttonStyle(.bordered)
            }
            if let trouble {
                Text(trouble)
                    .font(.footnote)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
        }
        .padding(.horizontal)
        .padding(.vertical, 8)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
        .background(.bar)
        .tint(Color(.adminAccent))
    }

    /// Why the shelf is empty, when it is for a reason a grown-up can act on.
    private var trouble: String? {
        guard let failure = session.appleLibrary.lastFailure else { return nil }
        if failure is AppleLibraryUnavailable {
            return "Sync Library is off for this Apple Music account, so there's nothing to show here."
        }
        return "Your Apple Music library couldn't be read just now."
    }
}
EOF

/// One song in a playlist. Always a song — see ``PlaylistRow``.
public struct PlaylistEntryRow: Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable {
    public let id: UUID
    public let catalogID: CatalogID
    public let displayName: String
    public let artworkURL: URL?

    /// 0-based and contiguous. Gaps are not a supported state.
    public let position: Int
    public let addedAt: Date

    /// Always a song, so empty always means unresolved, not inapplicable.
    public let ancestry: LibraryAncestry

    public init(
        id: UUID,
        catalogID: CatalogID,
        displayName: String,
        artworkURL: URL? = nil,
        position: Int,
        addedAt: Date,
        ancestry: LibraryAncestry = .none
    ) {
        self.id = id
        self.catalogID = catalogID
        self.displayName = displayName
        self.artworkURL = artworkURL
        self.position = position
        self.addedAt = addedAt
        self.ancestry = ancestry
    }
}

/// Entries are always songs — an album or artist is ambiguous to queue.
public struct PlaylistRow: Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable {
    public let handle: PlaylistHandle
    public let name: String
    public let createdAt: Date
    public let modifiedAt: Date

    /// True only when this app created the Apple counterpart; never inferred.
    public let appleIsOurs: Bool

    public let origin: LibraryOrigin

    /// Sorted by ``PlaylistEntryRow/position``. The order is the content.
    public let entries: [PlaylistEntryRow]

    public var id: UUID { handle.local }

    public init(
        handle: PlaylistHandle,
        name: String,
        createdAt: Date,
        modifiedAt: Date,
        appleIsOurs: Bool,
        origin: LibraryOrigin,
        entries: [PlaylistEntryRow]
    ) {
        self.handle = handle
        self.name = name
        self.createdAt = createdAt
        self.modifiedAt = modifiedAt
        self.appleIsOurs = appleIsOurs
        self.origin = origin
        self.entries = entries
    }
}

    /// The account holder's own playlists, snapshotted track by track.
    ///
    /// Apple's — mixes, stations' playlists, anything with a `kind` — are left
    /// out: they are recommendations wearing a playlist's clothes, and the
    /// catalogue they reach is nobody's choice. A playlist has no code, so the
    /// same handle on every read comes from its library id, hashed; without
    /// that the merge would see a new playlist each time. Not ours, ever —
    /// `appleIsOurs` is written only at creation, and this app created none.
    private func readPlaylists() async throws -> (rows: [PlaylistRow], unresolved: Int) {
        var rows: [PlaylistRow] = []
        var unresolved = 0
        let playlists = try await source.libraryPlaylists(limit: limits.playlists)
        for playlist in playlists where playlist.isPersonal {
            let tracks = try await source.tracks(of: playlist)
            let matched = try await source.resolveToCatalog(tracks)
            await cache?.store(Array(matched.matches.values))

            var entries: [PlaylistEntryRow] = []
            for track in tracks {
                guard let match = matched.matches[track.id] else {
                    unresolved += 1
                    continue
                }
                // Position, not the track: the same song twice is two rows.
                entries.append(
                    PlaylistEntryRow(
                        id: Self.stableID(for: "\(playlist.id)#\(entries.count)"),
                        catalogID: match.id,
                        displayName: match.title,
                        artworkURL: match.artworkURL ?? track.artworkURL,
                        position: entries.count,
                        addedAt: track.addedAt ?? .distantPast,
                        ancestry: learned[match.id] ?? Self.ancestry(of: match, named: track)
                    )
                )
            }
            rows.append(
                PlaylistRow(
                    handle: PlaylistHandle(
                        local: Self.stableID(for: "playlist:\(playlist.id)"),
                        appleLibraryID: playlist.id
                    ),
                    name: playlist.name,
                    // The library gives no dates for a playlist; none are invented.
                    createdAt: .distantPast,
                    modifiedAt: .distantPast,
                    appleIsOurs: false,
                    origin: .appleLibrary,
                    entries: entries
                )
            )
        }
        return (rows, unresolved)
    }

                // which is the gesture a kid already knows from rearranging

                }
            }
        }
        .sheet(isPresented: $isRenaming) {
            NamePlaylistSheet(
                session: session,
                renaming: handle,
                initialName: playlist?.name ?? ""
            )
        }
        // A playlist is the record in the store with the most of a kid's own work
        // in it. One tap should not be able to end it.
        .confirmationDialog(
            "Delete this playlist?",
            isPresented: $isConfirmingDelete,
            titleVisibility: .visible
        ) {
            Button("Delete", role: .destructive) {
                Task {
                    trouble = await session.deletePlaylist(handle)
                    if trouble == nil { dismiss() }
                }
            }
        }
        .task { await load() }
        .onChange(of: playlist?.modifiedAt) { _, _ in Task { await load() } }
    }
