+
A fourth used to be on that list and is now conditional. **The user's own library
is not a browsing source unless the library is the kid's own**, which is what
`isSharedDevice == false` asserts — and that is the default, so the amendment is
in force from first launch. Three things carry the original protection across:
onboarding asks before the Apple provider's first read, the policy engine judges
every item read back, and the read happens only through `LibraryProvider`, so
there is one place the door opens rather than a call site per screen. The
library as a *seeding input* for a parent building lists is untouched — that is
still `LibrarySource`, still ISRC/UPC matching, and no part of it runs through
`KidLibrary`.

**There is a second exception, and it is the grown-up's, not the kid's.** On a
shared device — `isSharedDevice == true`, hand-me-downs included — a grown-up
behind the passcode can take the player: **grown-up mode** reads their own
Apple Music library and nothing of the kid's, judges against an engine that
allows everything, and writes nothing to any kid's log, Recent shelf or report.
`Session.audience` is the switch and `LibraryLiveness` is the one table that
turns the device answers and the audience into which providers open; the
merge and the admin's health line both read it, so they cannot disagree. The
mode ends only by the band's button — not on background, not on a timer — so a
device left on a table stays walls-down until someone taps it, and the band is
what says so. Reading the library is all this stage does: **nothing is written
to Apple Music and nothing read from it is adopted into our store**, so an
Apple row lives exactly as long as the account keeps the item, and the heart
means "kept in this app" — an Apple-only song shows with the heart open until
the kid taps it. Songs and albums are read, newest first up to a cap;
artists are derived from song lineage, as they are for our own rows.

- writeSlot: Author one of the REQUIRED SLOTS seeded on every spec (see the page description for the list and what each owes). `markdown` replaces that slot section's body. This is the drafting agent's main verb: a new spec is born with every slot present and empty, and `submitForRestatement` refuses while any is blank. A page predating the rubric carries no slot sections; writing one CREATES it at the end, so an older spec grows its rubric a slot at a time instead of dead-ending at the gate.
- draftSection: Draft one spec section BEYOND the required slots — the spec's own material, or a subsection under a slot. Born ai-draft, awaiting human restatement. `markdown` is the section body (full block Markdown). `depth` is the outline level: 0 is a top-level section, 1 a subsection of the section above it (it may not skip a level). Appends unless `afterId` names an existing section to insert immediately after — which is how you put a subsection under its parent.
- indentSection: Make a section a SUBSECTION of the one above it — it and its own subsections all shift one level deeper. Pure structure: no content changes and a human-verified section stays verified. Refused when it would skip a heading level (nothing above to nest under) or on a required-slot section, which stays top-level.
- outdentSection: Promote a subsection one level toward the top — it and its own subsections all shift one level shallower. Sections that followed it at its old depth become its children. Pure structure: verified sections stay verified. Refused on a section already at the top level.
- restateSections: THE human accept (studio only — never call as the drafting agent): atomically replace the sections named in `removeIds` with the human's restated `sections`, which are born human-verified. The new run sits where the first removed section sat; an empty `sections` is a deliberate removal/shortening. Fails loudly when a removeId no longer exists (a concurrent edit won the race).
- acceptSections: HUMAN sign-off only (studio — never call as an agent, on the user's behalf or otherwise): accept the named ai-draft sections AS-IS, with no restatement. Reading the draft and judging it correct as written IS the verification; each section flips to human-verified with no content change. Fails loudly when an id is missing or not ai-draft.
- unacceptSections: Human-driven UNDO of acceptance: send the named human-verified sections back to ai-draft with NO content changes (they rejoin the restatement queue). An agent wanting to change verified content uses reviseSection instead. Fails loudly when an id is missing or not human-verified.
- reviseSection: AI/system edit of an existing section's body (and optionally title). A human-verified section is honestly downgraded to ai-draft in the same commit — it must be re-verified by restatement.
- addSection: HUMAN authoring (studio only — the drafting agent uses draftSection): insert a section the human WROTE, born human-verified because their own words ARE the verification. Appends unless `beforeId` names an existing section to insert immediately before (that anchors the position to an id, so a concurrent insert elsewhere can't shift it).
- moveSection: Reorder: move a section — WITH its subsections, which travel as one block — to 0-based `toIndex` among the sections remaining once the block is lifted out. Pure structure: no content and no status change, so human-verified sections stay verified where they land. The block's depth is clamped to what the destination allows (a subsection moved to the top of the spec becomes a top-level section), so a move can never leave a skipped heading level behind.
- removeSection: Delete a section outright — the human's call that this content does not belong in the spec. Its subsections go with it, and unlike join and split, which preserve one id, the ids are GONE: a restatement in progress on any of them goes too. Refused on a required-slot section, and on any section whose subtree holds one — a slot is an obligation, not a suggestion.
- joinSections: Merge `absorbId` INTO the section immediately before it: `sectionId` keeps its id, title and position and its body gains the absorbed blocks; `absorbId` is removed. Ids survive on purpose — a restatement in progress on the survivor outlives the join. Provenance stays honest: the survivor keeps human-verified only when BOTH were verified; absorbing an ai-draft returns it to ai-draft.
- splitSection: Split one section in two: `sectionId` KEEPS its id, title, position and status but its body becomes `topMarkdown`, and a new section titled `newTitle` holding `bottomMarkdown` is inserted immediately after it, born with the SAME status (splitting your own verified words leaves both verified; splitting an ai-draft leaves two ai-drafts). The surviving id means a restatement in progress on the top half outlives the split. `asSubsection` makes the bottom half a SUBSECTION of the top rather than its sibling — the split that turns one long section into a parent and its first child.
- recordHolisticReview: Record the holistic AI review — summary plus notes (born open) — and fire the page's requestHolisticReview transition to reviewing, all in ONE commit. Requires every section human-verified.
- rerunHolisticReview (not currently legal): Re-run the holistic review while reviewing (after sections changed): replaces the summary and every still-open note with fresh ones; resolved notes are kept as history. Requires every section human-verified again. No page transition.
- resolveNote: Resolve one open review note, optionally recording how it was addressed.
- submitForRestatement (not currently legal): Declare the AI draft complete and hand the spec to the human for restatement. Refused until the rubric holds: every required slot authored, the data-model slot carrying actual types, the invariants slot a list, and every `(see X)` naming a section that exists.
- completeRestatement (not currently legal): Move a fully-restated spec to `restated`. - reopenRestating (not currently legal): Escape from reviewing back to restating (e.g. the review invalidated the restatement pass).

Mutations for document:ms3de6rj-0028-3cfe24 (document):
- setMarkdown: Replace the entire body with parsed Markdown (paragraphs, headings, lists, fences, quotes, tables).
- addParagraph: Append a paragraph of inline runs (pass `index` to insert at that position). A run is a plain string; {text, bold?, italic?, href?} for bold/italic/link-marked text; {code} for an inline code span; or {ref: pageId} for an integrity-checked page reference whose label is render-derived (a dangling pageId aborts the commit). Markdown syntax inside a text run is rejected — express it as runs instead.
- addHeading: Append a heading at `level` 1–6 of inline runs (pass `index` to insert at that position).
- addCode: Append a fenced code block (pass `index` to insert at that position). The content hash is recomputed at ingestion; later edits go through the generated applyBodyBodyBlockEdits under `expectedHash`.
- addList: Append a list — `ordered` true renders 1./2./3., false renders bullets; each item is one paragraph of inline runs (pass `index` to insert at that position).
- addQuote: Append a block quote of one or more paragraphs, each an array of inline runs (pass `index` to insert at that position).
- addTable: Append a table: `header` is one cell (an inline-run array; [] for an empty cell) per column, `rows` matching the header width, optional `align` per column (left/center/right/null; defaults to null). A width mismatch rejects the commit (pass `index` to insert at that position).
- addDivider: Append a horizontal divider (pass `index` to insert at that position).
- addImage: Append an image (pass `index` to insert at that position). `ref` is either `attachment:<sha256>` — bytes uploaded to this wiki's attachment store, which the event stream references but never carries — or an ordinary absolute URL. `alt` is the description a reader gets when the image cannot be shown, so write it as one; it is not a caption.
- setImage: Replace an IMAGE's ref, alt and title in place (same block id, position unchanged); rejects any other block kind.
- setParagraph: Replace a PARAGRAPH's inline runs in place (same block id, position unchanged); rejects any other block kind.
- setHeading: Replace a HEADING's level and inline runs in place (same block id, position unchanged); rejects any other block kind.
- setList: Replace a LIST's `ordered` flag and items in place (same block id, position unchanged); rejects any other block kind.
- setQuote: Replace a QUOTE's paragraphs in place (same block id, position unchanged); rejects any other block kind.
- setTable: Replace a TABLE's header/rows/align in place (same block id, position unchanged); rejects any other block kind.
- moveBlock: Move an existing block to `toIndex` within the document order.
- removeBlock: Remove a block by id (an unknown id rejects the commit).
- setBodyBody
- applyBodyBodyBlockEdits

    "slot": "invariants",
    "markdown": "- **This is the kid's library only.** Nothing here is reachable from the admin, and the admin's existing library seeding (`LibrarySource`, ISRC/UPC matching for allow and deny lists) is neither used by it nor changed by it.\n- **Neither a favorite nor a playlist entry is a permission.** Nothing here creates a `PolicyEntry` or changes a verdict. The policy engine remains the single authority.\n- **A kid may only favorite, or add to a playlist, what they may currently play.** Every write asks the engine first and refuses a blocked item.\n- **Everything read back is filtered at render time, never stored pre-filtered.** A parent may deny tomorrow what the kid favorited today: the row survives, the tile does not.\n- **Playlist entries are always songs.** Albums and artists can be favorited but never added to a playlist — what would play is ambiguous, and the player queues songs.\n- **`isSharedDevice` and who is looking are the only inputs to which providers are live**, and `LibraryLiveness` is the one table that turns them into an answer — the merge and the admin's health line both read it, so they cannot disagree. For the kid: false (the default) is both, true is CloudKit alone. For a grown-up: the Apple library alone, whatever the device answers say. There is no other gate and no derived trust state.\n- **`isSharedDevice` defaults to false, is device-local, and never syncs.** It describes a device and the library on it, not the family.\n- **The Apple provider's first read is not issued until onboarding has asked.** The default decides what happens if that question is never answered; it must not decide what happens before it is put. The app's own refresh is gated on the same table, so a grown-up's library on a shared device is never read into memory, drawn or not.\n- **CloudKit is always live for the kid.** Every operation therefore has at least one provider, and the feature is complete with Apple Music absent. For a grown-up it is set aside — reported as an answer given, not a fault.\n- **Reads never write.** Nothing read from the Apple library is adopted into our store, and no read prunes, contradicts, or writes back into another provider. An Apple row lives exactly as long as the account keeps the item.\n- **A read is a union, and CloudKit only ever expands it.**\n- **The heart draws only from rows the kid can act on.** A row read from the Apple library alone shows on the shelf with the heart open; a tap makes it a kept one in our store. A filled heart that no tap could empty is a dead control.\n- **Callers never name a provider.** Every surface talks to the merged store.\n- **A capability a provider lacks is not an error.** It sits that operation out and the others carry it. Only a provider *failing* something it claims to support is a failure. The Apple provider declares none, so it sits every write out.\n- **Nothing a grown-up does is written.** Not a play, a search, a block or a visit; the Recent shelf and the parent's suggestion shelves answer empty; the report shows no row from their session. Reporting runs in all three levels and not in grown-up mode.\n- **Grown-up mode ends only by its button.** Not on background, not on a timer. A device left on the table stays walls-down until someone taps it, and the band on every kid screen is what says so — the one thing on the kid's side that names a provider state.\n- **Drift between providers is not reconciled.** An item in CloudKit and not in Apple Music stays that way. A deliberate limit, not an oversight.\n- **Absence from the Apple Music library never deletes a CloudKit row.**\n- **The CloudKit write is awaited and surfaced; the Apple Music write is fire-and-forget.** (Writing has not shipped; the rule is written down ahead of it.)\n- **Every stored identifier is an Apple Music catalog identifier.** Items read from the Apple Music library are resolved by ISRC and UPC first; anything that will not resolve is dropped rather than stored under a library identifier — and counted, because the rate is open question 2.\n- **`appleIsOurs` is written at creation and never inferred.** Every playlist read from the library is not ours.\n- **An edit is never attempted on a playlist we did not create.**\n- **Favorites and playlists are exempt from event retention.** Plans and searches are events and may roll into summaries; these are durable user data, deleted only by the kid or with the kid.\n- **Nothing about provider availability is ever shown to a kid.** Capability gaps and provider failures are admin-facing. The grown-up band is the exception, and it is shown to the grown-up.\n- **`MusicLibrarySearchRequest` is not used** for the kid's library search.\n- **Artwork bytes are never copied into our storage.** `artworkURL` is a reference; `displayName` is a copied string so a list renders offline."

}

    "depth": 0,
    "markdown": "Added 2026-09-02, with the reading stage. The shared-device toggle above says the library signed in on a shared device is a grown-up's and the kid must not see it. It said nothing about the grown-up, who until now had no way to listen to their own music in this app at all.\n\n**What it is.** On a device where `isSharedDevice` is true — a shared device, or a hand-me-down still signed in to a parent's account — a grown-up behind the passcode can take the player. It is offered in the admin's device section, beside the two answers that decide whether it is offered, and it closes the admin with it. A dedicated kid device never offers it: the library there is the kid's own and already on their shelf.\n\n**Three decisions, each the maintainer's.**\n\n1. *The Apple library only.* Not the union with the kid's CloudKit rows. The kid's favorites and playlists are theirs, and a grown-up's shelf that showed them would be either the kid's private list on the wrong screen or an invitation to edit it.\n2. *Walls down, nothing logged.* The same rule the admin's preview methods keep, enforced as one switch — `Session.audience` — on every path that writes under the kid's id, rather than as a parallel set of methods, because the grown-up uses the kid's screens.\n3. *It ends only by the button.* Not on background, not on a timer. A parent listening with the screen off is the case it exists for. The cost is stated plainly: a device left on the table stays walls-down until someone taps \"Back to kid mode\", and the band on every kid screen is what says so. That band is the one exception to \"nothing about provider availability is ever shown on the kid's side\", and it is shown to a grown-up.\n\n**How it holds together.** `LibraryAudience` joins `isSharedDevice` as the second input to `LibraryLiveness`, the one table the merge and the admin's health line both read. `rebuildEngines()` is the only builder and asks who is looking, because every policy edit, kid switch, dismissal and sync-driven clear comes through it, and one that rebuilt for the kid mid-session would put the walls back up under a band still saying they are down. The player's queue owner is optional: a grown-up has no slot, so their queue is neither written into the kid's nor put back on the next launch, and leaving clears it *before* the kid's engine is rebuilt — otherwise the re-check that rebuild triggers would judge the grown-up's track under the kid's policy and write a block in the kid's name for a song the kid never heard. Entering the admin leaves the mode first: the admin is about a kid.\n\n**What is absent for a grown-up.** The heart, the favorite button, the add-to-playlist control, and the playlist screen's drag, swipe, rename and delete. Absent rather than disabled: their only provider is read-only and the kid's store is set aside, so a tap would land nowhere, and a heart that fills for nobody is a lie the kid's heart never tells."

  "workspaceId": "ws:ms3de17i-0024-ik1oty",
  "pageId": "spec-restatement:ms4lu92o-01op-x3xmw",
  "command": "draftSection",
  "args": {
    "title": "Reading before writing, and no adoption",
    "depth": 0,
    "markdown": "The staged plan first put writing before reading and had every read adopt what it found into CloudKit as `origin: appleLibrary` rows. The reading stage shipped 2026-09-02 the other way round on both counts, and this section records why so the Algorithm and Migration sections above — which still describe adoption — read as the earlier plan rather than the current code.\n\n**Reading first**, because it is the half that changes what a kid sees and it needs no capability the framework might refuse. The provider declares no capabilities, so every write path in the merge already sits it out, and writing can arrive later as flags without touching a caller.\n\n**No adoption**, by decision. A read is now a snapshot the provider holds in memory, served to every caller and refreshed behind the app; nothing read from the Apple library is ever stored. What that buys: no row in our store whose truth depends on another store; no adoption pass that could pull a grown-up's library onto a child's shelf, which the Migration section names as the one way this feature could go badly wrong; and no schema surface for the writing stage to inherit. What it costs: the shelf empties if the library becomes unreadable — Sync Library off, no network — and the admin's health line says which; and `ReviewedLibrary.adopted` and the `origin: appleLibrary` doc comment now describe rows read this pass rather than rows adopted, a wording gap left rather than churned.\n\n**Two consequences worth stating.** The heart draws only from rows the kid can act on: an Apple-only song shows with the heart open, and the tap makes it a kept one in our store, because a filled heart that no tap could empty is a dead control. And a level 1 kid on a dedicated device blocks their whole Apple library as `notOnAllowList` — the policy working, on a review screen that was not built expecting the volume.\n\n**Caps and what is not read.** Songs and albums come newest first up to constants in the provider (500 and 200 until a real library is measured); playlists are the account holder's own, up to 25, each costing a request for its tracks. Library artists are not read: they have no code and cost two requests each to vote on, and the browser derives artists from song lineage as it does for our own rows. Lineage is named from the library side at read time — the match carries the ids, the library row carries the album title and artist name — so the merge's top-up leaves these rows alone, and every matched item is put in the shared item cache as pages land so the shelf's own lookup finds it warm."
  }
}

The Apple library read announces itself, since it fills no heart

The shelves reload when `favoriteIDs` changes, and the Apple library read
never changes it: those rows are kept out of the heart on purpose, so a kid
with two favorites still has two after five hundred songs arrive, and a
grown-up has none before and after. The read completed and nothing redrew
until something else happened to reload the home screen.

So the read bumps a generation the shelves watch, once, when the snapshot
has changed hands — not on every `refreshLibrary()`, or every heart tap
would load the shelf twice — and the band reads the failure through the
session for the same reason, the provider not being observable.

And the kid switch takes its queue owner from the same rule the mode change
does. A sync-driven binding change can switch kids under a grown-up, and
their queue must still belong to nobody.

Decisions to be aware of - Grown-up mode has no timeout. The band is the only signal that the walls are down. - Deep libraries are capped at 500 songs, 200 albums and 25 playlists, newest first, as constants in the provider. - The heart means "kept in this app".
